  "aggregated_output": "{\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag42\\\\full\\\\codex-381\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\native-tools.md\", \"sha256\": \"ffb63e46c4625cdca42c43b13664d5dc5368e7cb1394edc24cf697b6d2d1b6a8\", \"bytes\": 8664, \"text\": \"# Native test tools\\n\\nUse `selection.json` for the exact `approved_shell_argv_prefix` and absolute\\ninput/output paths. Append one helper operation per shell call. Use native\\nWrite/Edit for files; read with native Read or the documented `read-text` helper.\\nPrefer one `read-text` call for independent files whose exact paths are known.\\nKeep normal permissions: no wrappers, loops, pipes,\\ndirectory listing, direct client commands or permission changes. This index\\ndescribes capabilities; it supplies no workflow or finished artifact.\\n\\nAll records, their companion evidence and export destinations must be new paths\\nunder the selected `work/` directory. The helper refuses other output locations\\nbefore executing the command. Use absolute paths from the selection; relative\\npaths resolve from the native workspace root, so include `work/`.\\nThe observation index scans that same `work/` directory only.\\n\\n## Draft mutations\\n\\nPrefer typed input for the operations below. This table supplies their CLI fields;\\nyou do not also need their raw schemas or help files unless a needed field is\\nmissing. Choose the operation, target, versions, key and content yourself.\\n\\n```text\\nremote OPERATION --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD [FIELDS]\\n```\\n\\nEvery typed mutation takes `--operation-key KEY --expected-project-version N\\n--evaluator-file FILE`. Use the selected `evaluator_file` path. The fixed adapter\\nsupplies the selected endpoint/project/token environment and exact installed\\nclient wheel. The client constructs the existing request and verifies its identity.\\n\\n| Operation | Other fields |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `import` | `--source-manifest FILE`; use selected `source_manifest` |\\n| `draft-open` | `--baseline ID --work-order WO-ID` |\\n| `create-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --domain NAME --artifact-type TYPE`; optional `--artifact ID --include-document` |\\n| `revise-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --document-file FILE` |\\n\\nHosted `create-artifact` allocates the ID and writes the draft in one operation.\\nIt has no `--dry-run` option; the local repository preview command does not apply.\\n\\nThe client never refreshes a version or retries a mutation on its own. Typed and\\nraw input cannot be mixed. Documents are exact UTF-8 files. No manual base64 or\\ncopied client digest is needed. `--include-document` adds one read of the exact\\ncreated revision, returning text or a decoded file path. Inspect it before editing.\\n\\n`--record` retains the command. Its new `.evidence` directory retains exact\\nrequests/responses and decoded documents. The displayed `client_view` is the\\nclient's own view. Inspect outcomes and findings; read required omitted content.\\nDo not reread a whole receipt just to extract a small field already displayed.\\nA capture error after send can leave a committed effect. Reconcile its original\\nkey with `remote operation --key KEY --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\n\\n## Read one revision\\n\\n```text\\nremote read --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --context UUID --context-version N\\n```\\n\\nFor an imported baseline, replace the context fields with `--baseline ID`.\\nReads take no `--operation-key`, `--expected-project-version` or `--evaluator-file`.\\nChoose the exact revision and context from the selected inputs or actual results.\\n\\n## Reads and discovery\\n\\n| Need | Operation |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Service readiness and selected components | `remote status --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` |\\n| Local wheel metadata | `identity` |\\n| Captured calls, reads and failures so far | `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`; retains the full snapshot and returns its field pointers, no content verdict |\\n| Complete released instruction sections | `instructions --section \\\"RESOURCE_ID#HEADING\\\"`; repeat for up to 12 sections |\\n| One unknown input location | `find-file BASENAME --under RELATIVE_DIRECTORY/` |\\n| One exact inventory entry | `lookup-file RELATIVE_NAME` |\\n| One saved JSON field | `read-json ABSOLUTE_FILE --pointer '\\\"/field\\\"'`; omit pointer for root; optional `--keys` |\\n| A raw base64 field | Add `--decode-base64` to that field read |\\n| One text file or independent reads together | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE [ABSOLUTE_FILE ...]`; up to eight selected inventoried inputs, the launcher-pinned task.md, or work files, at most 64 KiB output |\\n| Recover a truncated text read | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE --offset 0 --limit 4096`; one file, character offsets; continue from next_offset until complete is true |\\n\\nFor `instructions`, use canonical IDs such as `docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#read-this-when`. The earlier `released-resources/` inventory prefix also works. Request known sections together. The public reader includes the selected file's exact entry conditions when present; read their applicable references before acting. It does not follow links or select the next action.\\nFor authoring checklists and the repeated released 0.22.1 continuation heading,\\nuse the exact selectors in the selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-drafts.md`.\\n\\nFor known paths, use them directly. Inventory names are relative to the staged\\ninputs directory: `released-resources/docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`,\\n`source/src/greeting.py`, `client-help/create-artifact.txt`. **Do not add `inputs/`\\nto these names.** Native Read takes the absolute path, not an inventory name.\\nA digest or lookup is not a content read. Batch independent reads when their exact\\npaths are known. Unknown headings must not be guessed;\\nread the named file once to locate its actual headings. Request known current\\nsections together and reuse unchanged content. A full inventory is not required.\\n\\nRead [Execution tools](native-execution-tools.md) when choosing a planned check\\nor executing an authorized one. The description establishes the available\\nassertion and evidence fields; reading it does not run a test. Source inspection\\nis not test execution, and drafting a verification contract grants no execution\\nauthority.\\n\\n## Other operations\\n\\nRaw mode remains `remote OPERATION --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\nUse it for operations without typed input, or when explicitly checking a raw\\ncontract. Original schemas are under `reference/server/contracts/`. Selected\\nschema views use `schemas/remote-v1/OPERATION.json` or `schemas/read-v1/OPERATION.json`.\\nEach view retains its original pointer/digest. Lifecycle test-copy schemas are\\nseparate; do not load them for drafting alone. `--key` reads a receipt, not a document.\\n\\nFor lifecycle rehearsal use `remote rehearse --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record\\nABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`. The helper supplies the direct client's `--test-copy` flag;\\ndo not add that flag yourself. The request still needs `test_copy: true`.\\nThe selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-test-lifecycle.md` provides exact\\nreleased section selectors and pointers to individual action schemas.\\nFor a handoff file, `encode-file ABSOLUTE_FILE` returns its actual byte count,\\nSHA-256 and base64 content. It takes no output flag. Copy those returned values\\nunchanged; do not compute or guess a replacement digest.\\n\\nUse `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` before the final report. Read its\\nselected fields as needed. `observed_content_reads` contains successful visible\\nread metadata; `file_reads` retains Claude Read attempts, including failures.\\nUse the observed trace instead of rebuilding it with inventory lookups. Missing\\nreads remain unknown; rereading now does not prove an earlier read. The capture\\nmay be incomplete, and subsequent report writes are not yet counted. Keep the\\nrecord path as evidence instead of copying every command. This supplies no draft\\ntext, content judgement or lifecycle decision.\\n\\nThe returned `record` is the exact JSON **file**, even when it has no extension.\\nUse its `read_arguments` with the approved helper prefix. Do not append a filename\\nor treat it as a directory. Add `--pointer` only to select a field in that file.\\n\\n`command_records` includes extensionless record names. Each row points to its\\noriginal capture and copies selected exact `response_fields`, including available\\nreceipt, outcome and provenance values. Rows are sorted by filename, not time.\\nUse an indexed row to locate evidence, then inspect its original request/result\\nfor the claim. The index does not select a handoff base or certify a retry.\\n\\nRetain failed calls and recoveries. Template admission is not a content review.\\nReport only inspected facts and actual outcomes; distinguish unresolved content\\nfrom a completed definition. Do not claim an exhaustive failure count from memory.\\n\"}\r\n",

\"sha256\": \"430ef9eab115f2410f03f7f21f628b382641b859d31da41661095d0f433cea72\", \"bytes\": 9455, \"text\": \"## Select the current step\\n\\nUse exact instructions already delivered with their source identity. Reading that\\ncontent satisfies its read instruction. Open its file only if required content\\nis missing, changed or no longer retained. A pointer alone is not content.\\n\\nComplete [Hosted selection](../../setup/references/hosted-context.md) once for\\nthe unchanged selection. Draft preparation grants no decision right or Git authority.\\n\\nMatch the request and existing confirmed context to the current step:\\n\\n| Available inputs | Read from the selected release |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| The intended outcome or scope still needs clarification | `docs/engineering/harness/DEFINE_CHANGE.md`: **Read this when**, **Before this action**, then **Describe the intended outcome**. Use **Define the limits of the change** when its inputs are available. |\\n| Confirmed outcome, scope and selected definitions; a definition draft is needed | `docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md`: **Read this when**, **Before this action**, then the requested type's procedure below. |\\n\\nThe clarification procedure produces transient discussion, not a formal artifact.\\nUse its requester-confirmation process and reuse an existing matching confirmation.\\nAn instruction to create a draft does not supply the inputs that procedure requires.\\nDo not import, open a draft context or create a template merely to ask a question.\\nFor a clarification stop, include three short parts in the final reply:\\n\\n- **Actions:** State whether any hosted change was attempted. Include observed\\n  failures or denials.\\n- **Known inputs:** Keep existing definitions and supplied scope limits.\\n- **Questions:** Ask only for missing facts needed now.\\n\\nThis retained reply is the transient report only if no hosted mutation command\\nwas invoked and the captured attempted-call record is complete. Refused or denied\\nmutation commands are still attempts. If capture is incomplete or its completeness\\nis unknown, use the saved report in **Report and recover** and state that limit,\\neven when no change was observed. The clarification reply\\nneeds no duplicate file or new lifecycle checkpoint.\\n\\nFor a requested intent, consult `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#intent`\\nwhen identifying missing content. Read other prerequisites when their stated\\ncondition applies. Before selecting artifacts, load the clarification procedure's\\nartifact and link references. Before drafting, use this type table:\\n\\n| Type | Drafting procedure |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Verification | **Define how the result will be verified** |\\n| Release or operating contract | **Prepare a release or operating contract** |\\n| Other definition | **Draft any missing definitions** |\\n\\nApply the drafting procedure's prerequisites, including\\n`ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity` and the type checklist. Use full type\\nnames such as `#intent`, `#verification`, or `#work_order`, not codes.\\n\\nFor a release contract in a private lifecycle test, the source fixture commit\\nis not the disposable Git candidate that verification will capture. Do not\\ncomplete or approve a contract with a guessed candidate. If the final candidate\\nis not yet known, defer completing and approving the contract. Take its exact\\n`candidate_commit` from the final verified VREC, complete the release scope and\\nevidence requirements, then obtain the contract's required decision. An explicitly\\nsupplied candidate constraint remains binding.\\n\\nThe released `harnessctl ... REPO` examples act on repository files. Hosted work\\nuses the selected tool index or `docs/notes/harnessctl-reference.md#concise-hosted-authoring`.\\nDo not combine their arguments. The canonical content rules still apply.\\n\\nObtain missing sections together from the selected resource root; batch independent\\nfile reads with known paths. Missing, ambiguous or changed sources\\nstop the affected action. For 0.22.1's repeated\\n`CONTINUE.md#continue-selected-work` title, read its unique `#procedure` parent.\\nLoad [lifecycle instructions](hosted-test-lifecycle.md) only for that task.\\n\\n## Check the inputs before writing\\n\\nCompare the requested type's required content with the request and definitions:\\n\\n| Content | Source or authoring authority |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| User problem, improvement, success measure, existing gap | Require a source that supplies it. A creation request supplies no missing fact. |\\n| Proposed method, check, evidence destination | Choose within the requested design scope; label it planned. |\\n\\nFor an intent, ask which change in the user's situation is needed and how the\\nowner will know it helped, when those inputs are missing. An audience name or\\nreplacement output alone does not answer those questions. Reuse supplied answers;\\ndo not invent a purpose or measure from an engineering activity or baseline.\\n\\nBefore claiming a coverage gap, read the applicable requirements, specifications\\nand verification contracts. Code or one same-type record cannot establish their\\nabsence. For a verification plan, derive expected values from definitions; name\\nthe check, pass condition and full proposed evidence path, including filename\\nand any work-order directory. In an environment with restricted execution tools,\\nread their capability descriptions before choosing the check. This is a planning\\nread, not test execution. Match the planned assertions, platform and evidence\\nfields to those tools. Do not infer a local test runtime from the service runtime.\\nIf a required condition cannot be assessed with the available tools, report that\\ngap before requesting approval; do not promise an unavailable check.\\n\\nState a missing required fact as a question and stop dependent writing. A partial\\ndraft may omit it and remain incomplete. Do not call an unsupported required claim\\na non-blocking observation. Report a type/outcome mismatch without changing type.\\n\\n## Author and submit\\n\\nChoose the operation, target, expected versions, retry key and content. Use the\\ndocumented typed fields and evaluator identity file; do not also load raw schemas\\nfor those fields. Import is operator-only and uses the complete source manifest.\\n\\nUse `--typed --compact --record-directory NEW_DIRECTORY`, or the selected helper's\\ndocumented permission route. Raw `--request FILE` needs its schema and referenced\\ndefinitions. Do not mix modes or manually encode typed documents. Freeze is\\nraw-only and grants no approval. Explicit IDs permit a new domain; automatic\\nallocation requires an existing domain with an evaluable ID token.\\n\\nInspect the created template through `--include-document` or\\n[an exact revision read](../../harness-orient/references/hosted-reads.md#read-one-hosted-revision).\\nFindings are not the document. Complete only supported content and review it\\nagainst the type checklist. Remove unsupported claims, duplicate checks and\\nconstraints absent from definitions. For every verification pass condition,\\nidentify the planned check that assesses it. Add a missing check or narrow the\\nclaim; an untested condition prevents a complete-content claim. Report this\\nreview separately from template checks.\\n\\nSubmit the complete UTF-8 file with `revise-artifact`. Apply that review to the saved\\ndocument, then inspect its versions, receipt and findings before another draft.\\n`revise-artifact` edits an editable draft, not an approved or imported record.\\nLifecycle history, decisions and evidence stay immutable. If a protected-record\\nrefusal occurs, stop that revision. Do not retry it with changed state, history\\nor content. A separate draft proposal does not amend or replace an accepted\\nrecord; use the selected release's amendment boundary and obtain any missing\\nauthority before dependent work. Resolve blocked reads first.\\n\\n## Report and recover\\n\\nFor the clarification reply, use **Select the current step**. Otherwise retain\\ncomplete requests/results and one short report outside the repository, including\\nafter a mutation attempt or uncertain effect. Read required omitted findings.\\nThe report contains:\\n\\n- **Content readiness:** complete, incomplete or blocked against the selected\\n  type checklist. Give the supported content or exact missing input; saving alone\\n  establishes no completeness.\\n- **Saved state:** selection, revision, versions and exact document/result paths.\\n- **Validation and review:** evaluator findings, independent content findings,\\n  captured command observations including recovered failures and denials, uncertain\\n  effects, and any returned procedure/step. Use mechanical observations before an\\n  exhaustive failure claim. Link original evidence; do not copy its inventories.\\n\\nDraft validation checks template shape and required links. `content_review`\\nbeing `not_assessed` means only that the evaluator did not assess content. It\\ndoes not invalidate your separate review; an empty `incomplete` list does not\\ncomplete it. Name the method: source inspection, executed test or evaluator check.\\nPlanned checks are not executed tests. Keep report and final reply consistent\\nabout readiness and actual checks. Use only confirmed paths/digests.\\nAfter compaction, recover the retained reply or report and obtain fresh context.\\n\\nFor stale input, inspect the selection without silently refreshing versions.\\nFor an uncertain reply or capture failure, look up `remote operation --key KEY`\\nwith the same selection and credential, or retry identical bytes and key. Resolve\\nthe effect before selecting another key. Changed bytes under an accepted key are\\nrefused. Never fall back to local writes.\\n\"}, {\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag42\\\\full\\\\codex-381\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\README.md\", \"sha256\": \"fbf52d7ea22bab1dc9e4441ed14900dac8707faee648c6291addc45d3186984e\", \"bytes\": 15576, \"text\": \"# Hosted artifact sandbox\\n\\nOne Python service provides HTTP commands and shared HTTP/MCP reads over one\\nMemgraph database. Git remains the repository's formal authority. The sandbox\\nimports a fixed snapshot and prepares drafts. The explicit Phase 3 test-copy mode\\ncan rehearse lifecycle actions on new test records. It cannot replace imported\\ndecisions or authorize real work or publication. RISK-HAG-001 remains raised:\\napplication query controls do not prove database-enforced read-only access.\\n\\nPhase 2 was verified in VREC-HAG-004. The private lifecycle pilot under WO-HAG-008\\nwas verified in [VREC-HAG-005](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification-records/VREC-HAG-005.md)\\nand integrated through PR #542. Its eight VER-HAG-006 scenarios passed.\\nThe separate native Codex/Claude qualification under WO-HAG-009 is\\n[in progress](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-009/report.md).\\nNo public service, release, authority cutover or production claim is supplied here.\\n\\n## Inputs\\n\\nUse a Linux/amd64 Docker engine with Compose and Python 3.11+ on the operator\\nhost. The service uses the immutable CPython 3.13.16 image in [Dockerfile](Dockerfile),\\nMemgraph 3.13.1 in [compose.yaml](compose.yaml), hashed [Python dependencies](requirements.lock)\\nand hashed [Git packages](system-packages.lock.json). Use only public test data.\\nKeep all outputs outside the checkout. Preserve volumes until restore comparison\\nand qualification finish. The API binds loopback; the database has no host port.\\n\\nThe governor is public evaluator 0.22.1, wheel SHA-256\\n`cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053`.\\nCandidate remote client 0.22.2 lives in another environment. Unpublished plugin\\n0.2.7 bundles the unchanged evaluator and matching remote guidance. Service\\n0.1.0.dev1 owns server dependencies; the core checker keeps zero runtime dependencies.\\n\\n## Build the exact combination\\n\\nCommit the reviewed implementation. Follow the existing\\n[release build sequence](../docs/notes/developing-se-harness.md#release-sequences)\\nto produce the 0.22.2 candidate wheel and its two-build replay JSON at that commit.\\nUse the public 0.22.1 wheel as `EVALUATOR_WHEEL`. Resolve uppercase placeholders\\nto absolute paths or selected values. Keep each path as one argument.\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/qualify.py prepare --repository REPO --output PACKAGE_OUT --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --client-replay CLIENT_REPLAY_JSON --evaluator-wheel EVALUATOR_WHEEL --image LOCAL_IMAGE\\n```\\n\\nThe command refuses a dirty checkout or client replay from another commit. It\\nreads exact Git blobs, uses the existing development plugin assembler, builds\\nthe service image, and records actual component identities. Outputs are:\\n\\n- `combination.json`: built identities, marked qualification pending.\\n- `configuration/config.json`: non-secret selection for that combination.\\n- `credentials.json`: generated test principals; keep this file private.\\n- `plugin/`: separate Codex and Claude development archives and extracted trees.\\n- `candidate-source/server/compose.yaml`: the selected deployment recipe.\\n- Command results and image metadata, including failures.\\n\\nReadiness verifies the selected release, installed service bytes, runtime,\\ndatabase version/configuration, schema and complete tuple. It is not assurance.\\n\\n## Stage the historical source\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/stage.py REPO REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/reference-manifest.json SOURCE_OUT\\n```\\n\\nThis writes `source/`, `source-manifest.json` and `source-inventory.json` from\\nexact Git blobs, including original code/evidence bindings. It does not execute\\nsource files. Create a new Docker volume `SOURCE_VOLUME` and copy those three\\nentries into its root. On Windows, archive the entries and extract inside Docker\\nto avoid slow small-file reads through a Windows bind mount. Retain the archive\\ndigest and copy command. Compose mounts this source read-only.\\n\\n## Initialize and start\\n\\nSet these environment variables for every Compose command:\\n\\n| Name | Selected value |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `HAG_SERVICE_IMAGE` | Built `LOCAL_IMAGE`; retain its inspected immutable identity |\\n| `HAG_HTTP_PORT` | An unused loopback port, for example `18080` |\\n| `HAG_SOURCE_VOLUME` | Populated `SOURCE_VOLUME` |\\n| `HAG_CONFIG_DIRECTORY` | Absolute `PACKAGE_OUT/configuration` |\\n| `HAG_CREDENTIAL_FILE` | Absolute `PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json` |\\n\\nChoose a new Compose project `PROJECT_NAME`. `COMPOSE_FILE` is the generated\\n`candidate-source/server/compose.yaml`.\\n\\n```text\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE up -d graph\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE run --rm service init\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE up -d service\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE exec -T service harness-hosted ready\\n```\\n\\nWait for database availability before initialization and service readiness before\\nclient operations. Initialization is explicit; ordinary startup does not migrate\\nor repair a schema. `/health` means alive; authenticated `/v1/status` means ready.\\n\\nInstall `CLIENT_WHEEL` with `pip --no-deps` into a separate disposable environment.\\nIts Python is `CLIENT_PYTHON`. Use `-I -m se_harness remote`, never that candidate\\nas the governor. Read the extracted plugin's setup **Hosted sandbox selection**,\\nthen harness-orient or change. Native host discovery must be tested separately\\nwhere required; extracting files does not prove a host loaded the plugin.\\n\\n## Test the actual packages\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_service.py --client-python CLIENT_PYTHON --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --configuration PACKAGE_OUT/configuration/config.json --credentials PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json --source-manifest SOURCE_OUT/source-manifest.json --scenario-fixture REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:PORT --output WALKTHROUGH_OUT\\n```\\n\\nThe packaged client imports and retries, retrieves the fixed work context, creates\\nand revises a draft, refuses invalid/stale writes, recovers a receipt, compares\\nviews, reads Cypher, runs the released check and freezes the draft. Each request\\nand result is retained. Its report lists remaining checks; it is not full acceptance.\\n\\nRun `tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_boundaries.py` with installed service\\ndependencies in a separate Compose service process. Mount the test directory\\nread-only and a new output directory. Pass `--walkthrough WALKTHROUGH_OUT` and\\n`--output BOUNDARY_OUT`. Default checks cover protected/malformed requests,\\nconcurrent connections, transaction faults, HTTP/MCP parity and resource limits.\\nFault hooks exist only in the test process, never on a network route.\\n\\nUse `--only lost_reply` with a separately installed candidate `--client-python`\\nand `--client-wheel` inside that process for lost-response recovery. If earlier\\nchecks advanced the context, pass their final `--continuation` JSON. Inspect the\\nretained operation before retrying any interrupted write. Never invent a new\\nexpected version or operation key to make a failed test succeed.\\n\\nRun `qualify_history.py` through the isolated released evaluator with `-I`, the\\nmounted original `--source`, `--manifest`, fixed `--fixture`, new `--output`, and\\nwalkthrough `005-work-context-result.json` as `--hosted-result`. This independent\\nprojection compares the evaluator result and recomputes legacy path/code hashes.\\n\\nFollow the complete [VER-HAG-001 matrix](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification/VER-HAG-001.md),\\nincluding import variants, missing bindings, tuple/schema failures, measured\\nlimits and native plugin observations. Skipped or absent cases are unperformed.\\nRun the applicable repository regression and distribution checks.\\n\\nRun `qualify_integrity.py` in a disposable service process with the same mounts,\\nwalkthrough and current continuation. Supply its separately installed candidate\\n`--client-python`. This checks altered deployment identities, installed service\\ncontracts, evaluator substitution, and broken context-base links. Its file edits\\naffect only the disposable container; its graph edits always roll back. Do not run\\nit inside the serving container. Passing these checks does not complete the other\\nscenario requirements.\\n\\nRun `qualify_imports.py` with the walkthrough, current continuation and a new\\noutput directory. It creates disposable copies of the original source to test\\nduplicate IDs and unresolved targets. It also rejects unsupported import formats\\nand changed bytes under the original provenance. These negative tests must not\\nchange the database.\\n\\n`qualify_time.py` measures the configured five-second database read-transaction\\nlimit. Its stress query is a direct driver test, outside the public read grammar.\\nIt must produce a resource-limit refusal. This does not by itself prove a slow\\nquery's HTTP response or replace the public Cypher admission checks.\\n\\n## Restart and restore\\n\\nKeep the same `HAG_*` environment and stop other test writers. Use a fresh output\\nand an unused restore port:\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/qualify.py recover --compose COMPOSE_FILE --project PROJECT_NAME --output RECOVERY_OUT --restore-port RESTORE_PORT\\n```\\n\\nThe command fingerprints the acknowledged graph, restarts the original, stops\\nwriters/database for a consistent backup, resumes the original, and restores\\ninto a new `PROJECT_NAME-restore` volume. It refuses an existing restore volume.\\nIt compares both copies at the cutoff and records times, storage, archive digest\\nand commands. Keep the backup and both volumes. Record the archive's retained\\nlocation outside Git. This proves no power-loss, production RPO/RTO or migration claim.\\n\\n## Protocol and limits\\n\\nSee the [protocol guide](../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md) and closed\\n[command](contracts/remote-v1.json), [read](contracts/read-v1.json) and\\n[result](contracts/result-v1.json) schemas. Views are explicit. Domain and MCP\\nreads share one handler. Partial reads cannot support a governing-context claim.\\n\\nLimits: 2,500 imported artifacts; 10,000 retained revisions; 1 MiB per document;\\n64 MiB of formal import content; two evaluator slots; 500 aggregate read rows;\\n2 MiB per response; depth eight; five seconds per Cypher query; 120 seconds per\\nevaluator process. Preserve measured limitations and RISK-HAG-001. Do not expose\\nthe sandbox on a shared or untrusted network.\\n\\n## Phase 3: private lifecycle rehearsal\\n\\nThis is an opt-in test project. Supplied decision actors are synthetic labels.\\nGit remains authoritative for real definitions and decisions. Authentication and\\ndatabase ACL implementation are deferred; keep the existing private controls.\\n\\n1. Build the clean candidate client with the pinned recipe above. Prepare the\\n   service with the same command above, adding `--phase3`. The configuration selects\\n   schema revision 2 and `test_copy: true`. These are local qualification packages;\\n   do not publish them or replace the user's installed plugin.\\n2. Create the small synthetic source fixture outside the checkout:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   python REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/prepare_lifecycle_fixture.py --evaluator-python RELEASED_PYTHON --output FIXTURE_OUT\\n   ```\\n\\n   `RELEASED_PYTHON` is the absolute Python path for public evaluator 0.22.1. This\\n   command uses `-I`, creates an ordinary disposable Git repository, validates the\\n   seed records and stages exact Git blobs. Copy `FIXTURE_OUT/staged/` into a new\\n   source volume with the volume procedure above.\\n3. Use a new Compose project and graph volume. Set `HAG_SERVICE_IMAGE`,\\n   `HAG_CONFIG_DIRECTORY`, `HAG_CREDENTIAL_FILE`, `HAG_SOURCE_VOLUME` and a free\\n   loopback `HAG_HTTP_PORT`. Start the stack and run its explicit `init`. Do not\\n   migrate or reuse a Phase 2 volume. Read authenticated status and require the\\n   expected package identities, schema revision 2 and `test_copy: true`.\\n4. Install `CLIENT_WHEEL` into a separate environment. Run the packaged-client\\n   walkthrough, keeping its output outside the checkout:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   python REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_pilot.py --repository REPO --client-python CLIENT_PYTHON --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --configuration PACKAGE_OUT/configuration/config.json --credentials PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json --source-manifest FIXTURE_OUT/staged/source-manifest.json --endpoint ENDPOINT --output WALKTHROUGH_OUT\\n   ```\\n\\n   The runner authors new test definitions, exercises a failed gate and an invalid\\n   edge, accepts definitions, starts work, records a paired risk/decision, retains\\n   handoff evidence, and prepares and assesses a test VREC and RLS. It repeats\\n   accepted requests, reads the resulting context and exports an earlier and a\\n   later baseline. Each command and actual result is retained. It does not claim\\n   the remaining fault, concurrency, recovery or independent replay checks passed.\\n5. Use the recorded v2 request files as examples for deliberate manual rehearsal.\\n   The [wire contract](contracts/lifecycle-v2.md) defines every allowed operation.\\n   Keep versions and input digest from the selected preview. After a lost reply,\\n   use the existing operation lookup before changing a key or input.\\n6. Export with an explicit new destination. The client creates `files/`,\\n   `history.bundle` and `manifest.json`. An `.incomplete` marker means the export\\n   must not be used. Clone the bundle into another new directory, compare every\\n   exported file byte-for-byte, then use released 0.22.1 there to validate and\\n   check the selected records. Keep the original test candidate P from the VREC;\\n   a later governance commit is not a replacement candidate.\\n\\nThe read-only MCP tools use the same exact selected test snapshots. Their results\\nare labeled `se-harness-graph-read/v2`; ordinary Phase 2 projects retain v1 results.\\nNo new writable MCP tool or external publication operation is present.\\n\\nPreserve test volumes until restart and restore checks finish. If Docker has no\\nautomatic subnet left, inspect its networks and host routes, then supply a Compose\\noverride with unused private subnets. Retain the override and effective Compose\\nconfiguration with the run. Keep the database private and HTTP bound to loopback;\\ndo not delete unrelated stacks to obtain address space.\\n\\nFor the required supplemental checks, run `qualify_pilot_store.py` and\\n`qualify_pilot_replay.py` from `tests/hosted_artifact_graph/` in the packaged\\nservice container. Copy the selected walkthrough output into that container;\\nuse `--state WALKTHROUGH_OUT/walkthrough.json --output STORE_RESULT.json` for\\nthe store runner and `--walkthrough WALKTHROUGH_OUT --output REPLAY_OUT` for\\nindependent replay. Both use the mounted configuration and credential files.\\nThe store runner injects faults locally; no fault-injection HTTP route exists.\\nIt tests actual transaction rollback, racing writers, retained receipts, bounds\\nand the 120-second evaluator deadline. Retain its result before continuing.\\n\\nThen run `qualify_pilot_transport.py` on the client host with the walkthrough's\\nclient, configuration, credential, source, repository and endpoint arguments.\\nSet a new `--output TRANSPORT_OUT` and `--state STORE_RESULT.json`. It drops one\\nreply after a real commit, retrieves the receipt and repeats the identical\\nrequest. Use the recovery command above afterward.   "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag42\\\\full\\\\codex-381\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"a2041b84342c2b2e4b5ec0f26e3a70702a894c57d9810855cfe514881e5a0c28\", \"bytes\": 13484, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe selected change lacks a definition, verification, release or operating contract.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"43fb74d3453a8d13b76f867e87622559941ae3672acbf2aa9c26d9e9e6fde02f\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore choosing a type, read [ARTIFACTS.md#artifact-types](ARTIFACTS.md#artifact-types) and [ARTIFACTS.md#artifact-locations](ARTIFACTS.md#artifact-locations). Before links, read [DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions](DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions). Before authoring, read [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and the exact type checklist linked in this file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"fef13ff697eca3188c35b224644f1baf22534d9cb30142f440882d170d28bc6c\"}, {\"heading\": \"draft-any-missing-definitions\", \"title\": \"Draft any missing definitions\", \"anchor\": \"draft-any-missing-definitions\", \"start_line\": 29, \"end_line\": 108, \"content\": \"### Draft any missing definitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The confirmed outcome, scope limits, and missing-definition list\\nfrom [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New drafts of the missing intents (INT), capabilities\\n  (CAP), requirements (REQ), specifications (SPEC), applicable architectures\\n  (ARCH), and required architecture decisions (ADR). None if no definitions\\n  are missing.\\n- **Domain files and directories:** The structure reported by\\n  `scaffold-domain`, created only if the selected domain is missing.\\n- **Transient working material:** The inventory updated with generated IDs\\n  and file paths. Retain it under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read `Design simplicity` in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n2. Select the domain for each missing definition from the inventory. For a\\n   missing domain, preview its creation with the domain commands below.\\n3. Inspect the proposed domain paths. Resolve any reported conflict before\\n   running the domain creation command.\\n4. Select the first missing artifact type from the table below. Skip types\\n   already covered by unchanged existing artifacts.\\n5. Run the artifact preview command. Inspect its type, destination path, and\\n   `allocated_id`.\\n6. Run the artifact creation command with that exact ID. If a conflict occurs,\\n   repeat the preview; do not overwrite an existing record.\\n7. Open the returned file. Complete its title, owners, dates, content, and\\n   declared links. Replace all template placeholders.\\n8. Apply `### Checklist` under the matching `## TYPE` heading in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n9. Read the completed draft. Record its ID and path in the inventory.\\n10. Repeat actions 4\\u20139 for each remaining missing definition.\\n\\n| Order | Artifact | TYPE | Content | Declared links |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| 1 | Intent (INT) | `intent` | Problem, intended outcome, affected users, and scope limits. | None required here. |\\n| 2 | Capability (CAP) | `capability` | The ability needed to achieve the outcome. | `derives_from` \\u2192 intent (INT). |\\n| 3 | Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | Observable behavior, conditions, and acceptance criteria. | `derives_from` \\u2192 capability (CAP). |\\n| 4 | Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | Detailed behavior, constraints, failure behavior, and checkable examples. | `specifies` \\u2192 requirement (REQ). |\\n| 5 | Architecture (ARCH), when applicable | `architecture` | Components, boundaries, and the architecture decision assessment. | `addresses` \\u2192 requirement (REQ); `conforms_to` \\u2192 specification (SPEC). |\\n| 6 | Architecture decision (ADR), when required | `adr` | Context, alternatives, chosen design, and consequences. | `decides` \\u2192 architecture (ARCH). |\\n\\nRecord an unresolved design choice for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). Do not present a recommendation\\nas an agreed architecture decision (ADR). Prepare verification contracts (VER)\\nin [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor a missing domain, use the first command in action 2 and the second only\\nafter reviewing the preview in action 3:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain REPO --domain DOMAIN --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain REPO --domain DOMAIN --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each missing artifact, use this **creation sequence** in actions 5\\u20136.\\nReplace `TYPE` with the table value. Replace `ARTIFACT-ID` in the second\\ncommand with the first command's `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nThe preview writes nothing and does not reserve an ID. Creation writes one\\nincomplete template and returns its path. Content completion is a separate\\nediting action. The JSON output does not contain the authoring checklist.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each missing definition has a completed draft with an ID and\\npath. Unresolved choices are identified. If no definitions are missing,\\nrecord `None needed` in the transient inventory.\\n\\n**Later use:** These definitions supply the verification contracts (VER) in\\n[Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified) and the governing links in work orders (WO) in [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Their acceptance\\nis handled in the authorization process.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c38865671a81429dd291d9f9bb333deae02a4098d4afcf034f293ee919e990e0\"}, {\"heading\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"title\": \"Define how the result will be verified\", \"anchor\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"start_line\": 109, \"end_line\": 165, \"content\": \"### Define how the result will be verified\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected requirements (REQ), specifications (SPEC), proposed\\namendments, and existing verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or updated verification contracts (VER) in\\n  `draft` where coverage is missing. None created or modified where existing\\n  contracts provide unchanged coverage. Accepted contracts remain unchanged.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused verification\\n  contracts (VER), any amendment proposals prepared through [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions), coverage\\n  gaps, and unresolved questions. Retain these under the same conditions\\n  as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read each selected requirement's (REQ) acceptance criteria and linked\\n   specifications (SPEC).\\n2. Compare those criteria with the existing verification contracts (VER).\\n3. Select unchanged contracts that cover the proposed behavior.\\n4. For each coverage gap, create a verification contract (VER) with the\\n   commands below, or use [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions) to propose an amendment to an existing one.\\n5. Complete `Requirement-to-evidence matrix`. For each requirement (REQ),\\n   record its ID, method, case or evidence, and pass condition. Use `test`,\\n   `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration` as the method.\\n6. Specify the inputs, platform, evaluator, and command or manual actions for\\n   each check. Derive expected results from the requirement (REQ) and\\n   specification (SPEC), not from candidate output.\\n7. Set `[relations].verifies` to the covered requirement (REQ) IDs.\\n8. Complete `Independence`, `Evidence retention`, and applicable assessment\\n   sections in each new or edited draft.\\n9. Apply `## verification` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n10. Retain questions about missing criteria or methods for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new verification contract (VER), run the creation sequence from\\n[Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions) with these arguments. Inspect the preview before creation; replace\\n`VER-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --id VER-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nNo harness command writes the verification method or pass criteria. The human\\nor agent completes that content. No verification record (VREC) is created here.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every selected requirement (REQ) has a defined verification\\nmethod and pass condition, or an explicit unresolved question. Each proposed\\ncheck identifies how to perform it and where its evidence will be retained.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) links these contracts to work orders (WO). The execution\\nand verification processes later perform the checks and assess the evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"16a9ea7323450e244b26edd2d1ad757048124b627bcfffa157c8b173f57f363c\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag42\\\\full\\\\codex-381\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}, {\"heading\": \"intent\", \"title\": \"intent\", \"anchor\": \"intent\", \"start_line\": 76, \"end_line\": 84, \"content\": \"## intent\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\\n- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\\n- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\\n- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"291e8274f0c400a3d2d1ecdd56f2c10d68ab6cb40f667076a034e44d87c05e42\"}, {\"heading\": \"capability\", \"title\": \"capability\", \"anchor\": \"capability\", \"start_line\": 85, \"end_line\": 93, \"content\": \"## capability\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\\n- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\\n- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\\n- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee6452eeeb618cbe10c941638e7f6be38d2709f53e169920c2d3d012c94ce978\"}, {\"heading\": \"requirement\", \"title\": \"requirement\", \"anchor\": \"requirement\", \"start_line\": 59, \"end_line\": 75, \"content\": \"## requirement\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\\n- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\\n- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\\n- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\\n- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\\n\\n### Guidance\\n\\nWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\\nsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\\nare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\\nhave a valid value when supplied.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"333872b200842af881c6c22cfcb0631897071421f423885b2702ac6b72c75770\"}, {\"heading\": \"specification\", \"title\": \"specification\", \"anchor\": \"specification\", \"start_line\": 94, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"## specification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\\n- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\\n- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\\n- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\\n- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\\n\\nMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\\nhelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\\nbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7aeefa5f4ed363ecdef5185d2b776c6fdd9146ece8e2bfd7ae1ee852f0acf6e1\"}, {\"heading\": \"verification\", \"title\": \"verification\", \"anchor\": \"verification\", \"start_line\": 126, \"end_line\": 135, \"content\": \"## verification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\\n- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\\n- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\\n- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\\n- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e6d36e5fe7a23845861e67079317f856b4f892d7f17c4f3d4dbdb4476edb7720\"}, {\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8d3be9bfae6d0679a08544ac587fa73e1a26e026d23373c29e1927e0803e7b8\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag42\\\\full\\\\codex-381\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"title\": \"Complete work scope\", \"anchor\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"start_line\": 47, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"## Complete work scope\\n\\nEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\\nMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\\nhave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\\nReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\\n\\nA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\\nforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. Use exact file paths\\nby default. Use a narrow existing component directory when the affected\\nfiles belong to that component. A matching directory does not authorize\\nunrelated behavior.\\n\\nPrepare this scope through\\n[Draft work orders](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\nDo not split predictable supporting changes into extra work orders merely\\nbecause they use different file types. A genuine expansion after approval\\nstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"021ca3cdecffebe415ce9df445c0c48e24a0acde7609d25220c0fb7d470e054e\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

Create a conditional\\nartifact only when its condition applies.\\n\\nFor an existing selected work order (WO), get its current state and next\\naction with:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nBefore implementation, check whether that work order (WO) and its linked\\ndefinitions are eligible to start:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\n```\\n\\nThe first command reports lifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint\\ngates. Reuse a requirement (REQ) only if its meaning stays unchanged.                                              |\\n| `specification`       | `SPEC-`   | Defines the detailed behavior, interfaces, constraints, and rejection conditions.                                                                                            | Each requirement (REQ) selected for implementation needs specification (SPEC) coverage.                                                                  |\\n| `architecture`        | `ARCH-`   | Defines system structure and boundaries needed to meet significant requirements (REQ).                                                                                       | An active architecture (ARCH) directly addresses a requirement (REQ) selected by the work order (WO).                                                    |\\n| `adr`                 | `ADR-`    | Records an architecture decision (ADR), the alternatives, and their consequences.                                                                                            | An applicable architecture (ARCH) declares that a significant decision is required.                                                                      |\\n| `verification`        | `VER-`    | Defines how requirements (REQ) will be checked and what counts as a pass.                                                                                                    | Each selected requirement (REQ) needs verification coverage. Completed scope does not authorize later work.                               |\\n| `verification_record` | `VREC-`   | Binds work orders (WO), verification contracts (VER), evidence, and one exact candidate commit for assessment.                                                               | When verification tied to a commit is required. Inspect the implementation and follow its callers, references and consumers.\\n   Check tests and fixtures, instructions and documentation, packaging and CI,\\n   and verification outputs where they apply. Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\\nbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\\n\\n```toml\\n[relations]\\nimplements = [\\\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nspecifications = [\\\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nverification = [\\\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\\nAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\\nfill a field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e5892787048f79f437b0395f9e1269152ce3d1d1b6fb28994f42849bd12a4f54\"}, {\"heading\": \"assurance-classification\", \"title\": \"Assurance classification\", \"anchor\": \"assurance-classification\", \"start_line\": 86, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"## Assurance classification\\n\\nEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\\n`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\\nor `not_required`.\\n\\nUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\\ncode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\\nor their links. These are examples of \\u201cchanged trusted state\\u201d: information or\\nbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\\nresult.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\\nA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\\norder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\\n\\nUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\\nverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\\nthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\\nor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\\nin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\\nsupporting evidence. The work records the decision; it does not reassess the\\nrelease.\\n\\nA work order (WO) that combines both kinds of work MUST be split or classified\\n`required`. `not_required` removes the obligation to prepare a new\\nverification record (VREC) for that work; it does not remove required checks\\nor the links to verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ad947ba93cfc84640c82a0b165448ce2c15f04beed36f65a3dc031e4287aab3\"}, {\"heading\": \"generated-outputs\", \"title\": \"Generated outputs\", \"anchor\": \"generated-outputs\", \"start_line\": 66, \"end_line\": 85, \"content\": \"## Generated outputs\\n\\nExisting scope rules admit the selected work order's own file, records that\\ndirectly verify or release that work order, and those records' declared\\nevaluator-evidence paths. This does not admit those records' parent directories.\\nThe selected work order's own packet directory is also already admitted by\\nthe existing scope rules; the planning report identifies that separate rule.\\n\\nList other planned evidence, review and log destinations explicitly in the\\nwork order's scope unless an existing rule covers them. A neighboring file\\nor a record linked only to another work order is not automatically admitted.\\nThe conditional rule for recording risks during execution remains unchanged;\\nit is not a blanket admission of future files during preparation.\\n\\nIf a future record's ID is not allocated, mark its destination as unresolved\\nand explain the relationship rule expected to cover it. Do not create a\\nrecord or invent an ID to complete the plan. Once the evaluator prepares\\nthe record, assess its actual returned record and evidence paths. An\\nunresolved destination is not an already covered file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"21cb2760e5cf61158c5d19cca2af8dbe727ecf3df32247987cc1636059bde3e9\"}]}]}\r\n",

Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"title\": \"Assess the proposed artifact package\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"start_line\": 32, \"end_line\": 83, \"content\": \"### Assess the proposed artifact package\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected work order (WO) IDs, proposed definitions, validation\\nresults, and existing decision records (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** A review list identifying the selected\\n  artifacts, their states, applicable checks, and reported blockers.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run validation for the repository.\\n2. Inspect each selected work order (WO) with the command below.\\n3. Read the work order (WO) and its returned reading manifest.\\n4. Review the governing definitions against the relevant checklists in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n5. Check that the proposed work has defined scope, verification coverage,\\n   assurance classification, and accountable humans for the required decisions.\\n6. List the blockers affecting the selected package. Keep unrelated findings\\n   separate.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint transition --target approved --json\\n```\\n\\nRead the result of each required check. A `pass` satisfies that check only;\\nit does not approve the artifacts or authorize implementation. If a required\\ncheck returns `fail` or `not_assessable`, report its identifier and stated\\nreason, then follow \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d Do not proceed with the\\naffected approval.\\n\\nThe last command evaluates work-order approval gates. A checkpoint-free\\n`check` only reports lifecycle context. Definition artifacts cannot be selected\\nwith `check`; their transition gates are evaluated by the previews in [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n\\nBefore proposing a definition for approval, resolve its template placeholders.\\nIf it contains an `Open decisions` section, confirm that no unresolved decision\\nremains before setting that section to `None`. Do not remove an unresolved\\nquestion merely to make validation pass.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected package has an explicit list of review findings\\nand approval blockers. No approval is inferred from these checks.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers) resolves the blockers. [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) presents the package for a\\nhuman decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2ea6b051236e13dd427317722d16ce7941ef5a4eb4789f7fdf568ab3d0cae3c0\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag42\\\\full\\\\codex-381\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORITY.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"da7202bf8d1beee631e9b4b5ba01c04b440fbf76d200ccbccbb8781a59f88431\", \"bytes\": 16163, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"decision-rights\", \"title\": \"Decision rights\", \"anchor\": \"decision-rights\", \"start_line\": 19, \"end_line\": 80, \"content\": \"## Decision rights\\n\\nA profile describes who performs an action. A decision right describes which\\naction that person or agent is authorized to perform. Being a Human does not\\ngrant every right in this table. Being an Agent grants none by itself.\\n\\nUse the artifact's recorded ownership and any existing explicit delegation to\\nidentify the accountable human. Resolve a team name or ownership label to the\\nhuman making this decision. A proposed `owners` value, an example actor name,\\nor authorship of a draft MUST NOT assign decision authority.\\n\\nApproval, verification acceptance, and release decisions MUST be made by an\\nauthorized human. An agent MAY prepare the material and apply that human's\\nrecorded decision when authorized to do so. Applying the decision does not\\nmake the agent its author. The selected IDs, reviewed content, target states,\\nand reason MUST still match the decision at apply time.\\n\\nThe following stable IDs name rights and operations, not additional profiles.\\nAll applicable gates remain required.\\n\\nThese DR-* identifiers come from the selected evaluator's decision-right\\ncatalogue. Use the right and exact action returned by that evaluator. Legacy\\nowner labels identify recorded accountabilities; they do not create additional\\nHuman/Agent profiles or assign a decision to a person by themselves.\\n\\n| Right ID                   | Accountable profile and authority                                                                                                  | Required input                                                                                                    | Result                                                                                               |\\n|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `DR-DEFINITION-DECIDE`     | Human authorized to decide the selected definition.                                                                                | Complete definition, exact proposed state, and required checks.                                                   | Decision on that definition only.                                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-SELECT`             | Human authorized to approve the work scope.                                                                                        | Complete governing chain, bounded work order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Completed scope, passing handoff checks, and retained evidence.                                                   | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent under the approval of every selected work order.                                                                    | Exact candidate, selected work and verification contracts, retained evidence, and passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept verification for the selected candidate.                                                                | Ready record, assessed evidence, and the exact verify, reject, or supersede decision.                             | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration or release-preparation path.                                                           | Exact candidate, destination, and coverage required by that path.                                                 | One path-specific instruction.                                                                       |\\n| `DR-RLS-PREPARE`           | Human authorizes the release inputs; a Human or Agent may release record only.                                                                |\\n| `DR-EXTERNAL-ACTION`       | Human authorized for the exact external action. A Human or Agent may execute the authorized operation.                             | Action, immutable target, destination, prerequisites, and recovery conditions.                                    | Authorization limited to that operation; the subsequent tool result records its actual effects.      |\\n| `DR-RELATED-RECORD-SELECT` | Human or Agent; no decision authority is needed for inspection.                                                                    | Exact existing artifact ID.                                                                                       | Read-only selection.                                                                                 |\\n| `DR-REMEDIATION-SCOPE`     | Human authorized to change the affected definition or work scope.                                                                  | Failed criterion and proposed bounded correction.                                                                 | Explicit authority for the revised scope.                                                            |\\n| `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`      | Human accountable for the artifact blocked by the decision; for a deviation, the human accountable for the affected specification. | Open or deferred decision, selected option or disposition, exact reason, and any required revisit trigger.        | Recorded disposition and any declared paired-risk effect. Other blocked artifacts keep their states. |\\n\\nFor a lifecycle decision, the `--decision` value identifies its actual\\ndecision-maker. When an agent applies a human decision, that value is the\\nhuman who made it. For start and completion under approved execution, it is\\nthe actual Human or Agent executor. Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. Preparation `--owner` values identify the preparation actor, not\\na future assurance or release decision-maker.\\n\\nFor `decide`, when an owner label differs from the actual human's identity,\\nuse `--authority-owner OWNER` only after establishing that human's authority\\nfor the exact decision. Keep `--decision ACTOR` as the actual human. The\\nevaluator checks that OWNER holds the existing decision right and records it\\nseparately as `authority_owner`. With the option absent, ACTOR must itself\\nmatch an eligible owner. The command does not authenticate either claim or\\ngrant consent. Do not infer a binding from the decision's own owners, an\\nearlier approval, Git configuration or the agent's identity.\\n\\nSilence, elapsed time, a commit, a pull request, tool execution, or a passing\\ncheck MUST NOT count as a human decision. A rejection MUST include a non-empty\\nreason. Supersession MUST name exactly one eligible successor. The decision\\nand its resulting state MUST remain specific to the selected artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ecaeb29429bcaa4eac99857f2f921e270c4865d1edeec96f536d09eb6c3130a\"}, {\"heading\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"title\": \"Delegation and separation\", \"anchor\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"start_line\": 111, \"end_line\": 133, \"content\": \"## Delegation and separation\\n\\nA human decision right may be delegated only to another human who is permitted\\nto hold it. The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. The result controls the reported scope,\\neffects, blockers, final state, required decision, alternatives, and next step.\\nThe human or agent MUST NOT recompute those fields.\\n\\nFor a human-readable report, lead with the outcome or required decision. The\\nwording and headings may vary, and empty fields may be omitted. The report\\nMUST preserve:\\n\\n1. The actual artifact IDs and whether the selected operation completed or\\n   was blocked.\\n2. The observed effects, separately from expected effects that did not occur.\\n3. Every exact blocker and every material non-effect. In particular, do not\\n   imply approval, a transition, verification, release, a Git action,\\n   publication, deployment, or operation that did not occur.\\n4. The final lifecycle state and the accountable human or agent. When a\\n   decision is required, name the exact decision and authority needed.\\n5. Exactly one current typed procedure step from the evaluator.\\n6. The command's argument values and boundaries, or the operative meaning of\\n   the suggested response.\\n\\nOnly complete alternatives declared by the workflow may be shown. Present them\\nseparately from the primary next step. Do not invent an effect, authority,\\nblocker, decision, or alternative. Do not add unrelated repository findings\\nto the selected result. Do not replace the returned next step with an\\nopen-ended question about what to do next.\\n\\nAutomation MUST read the structured JSON result. New results declare\\n`digest_format = \\\"machine-fields-v1\\\"`. This digest binds machine fields such\\nas candidate identity, scope, state, gates, and command arguments. Explanatory\\nwording is excluded. Older retained results keep their original digest format.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d12f5fc7e6190762622666754fde9b70e658249ceb41f2fdbf48e5e0edbd0f8f\"}]}]}\r\n",
