For draft edits, use [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and the selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists).\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n### Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The artifacts marked `amend` in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change) and the confirmed outcome\\nand scope.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Updated content in existing definition drafts where\\n  amendments are needed. Artifact IDs and lifecycle metadata are preserved.\\n  No accepted definition is modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** The amendment proposals and their effects\\n  on linked artifacts, or `None needed`. Retain these under the same\\n  conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read each definition marked `amend`.\\n2. Identify the exact section or rule requiring a change.\\n3. Write its proposed replacement text.\\n4. Record the artifact ID, path, current state, existing text, proposed text,\\n   and reason for the change in the amendment proposal.\\n5. List the linked artifacts whose meaning or checks would be affected.\\n6. If the definition is in `draft`, apply the content edit. Apply its type's\\n   checklist in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n7. If the definition is accepted, keep the replacement in transient working\\n   material for review. Identify the exact accepted version by its artifact\\n   ID, recorded state, and SHA-256 digest of its complete file bytes. Describe\\n   the proposed linked revision. Do not change the accepted record or its state.\\n8. Retain unresolved questions for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec).\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for proposing replacement text or editing draft\\ncontent. No accepted-definition transition is performed here.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each definition needing amendment has an explicit proposed\\nchange and impact description. Existing drafts reflect the proposed edits.\\nAccepted definitions remain unchanged. If none need amendment, record\\n`None needed` in the transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** The proposals inform verification planning in [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified) and the\\nreview of work orders (WO) in [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Dependent work cannot treat proposed\\nreplacement text as accepted authority.\\n\\n**Accepted-definition amendment boundary:** An amendment MUST create a linked\\nrevision and preserve the accepted version. The new revision MUST identify\\nthe exact accepted version it replaces. Its proposed changes and effects on\\nlinked work MUST be reviewed before approval. It MUST NOT govern work before\\nthe required human decision and supported activation have been recorded.\\nEarlier work and evidence keep their original definition references.\\n\\nThis release has no supported command and relation for creating\\nand activating this linked definition revision. Keep the proposal transient\\nand report that precise missing capability. Stop dependent authorization or\\nexecution until a released procedure can record the revision link, its human\\ndecision, and its effect on selected work. Do not edit the accepted file, add\\nan invented relation, or treat an unrelated new draft as its replacement.\\n\\n\\n## Read next when\\n\\nA missing supported revision mechanism blocks dependent work \\u2192 [RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked](RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked). The score describes the knowledge expected from the reader, not the quality or complexity of the document. -->\\n\\n> This is a non-authoritative reference to command syntax, actors and side\\n> effects. The selected released evaluator computes lifecycle states, allowed\\n> transitions, gates and next actions. Start with\\n> [ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md`, heading `read-by-task`), then use\\n> [CONTINUE.md](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md`, heading `continue-selected-work`),\\n> [decision rights](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md`, heading `decision-rights`) and\\n> [results](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/RESULTS.md`, heading `report-a-lifecycle-result`) when directed.\\n\\n## Invocation\\n\\nIn evaluator examples, `harnessctl` means the absolute Python executable of\\nthe repository's selected released evaluator followed by `-I -m se_harness`.\\nRun it from outside the checkout. `REPO` is the absolute repository path;\\nreplace placeholders before running a command. A failed result goes to standard\\n  output in both renderings; a code appears once per line.\\n\\n## Command inventory\\n\\n| Command | Principal actor | State effect | Intended use |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `remote` | authorized sandbox operator or author; reader for reads | explicit remote reads or bounded sandbox draft writes; no local fallback | use the separately installed unpublished client; see [Hosted sandbox client](#hosted-sandbox-client-unpublished) |\\n| `init` | repository owner or authorized agent | writes the complete standard harness into an absent or empty target; under `--json` an engine refusal exits 2 and a failed generation carries the engine's standard error in `error` |\\n| `resources` | human or agent | read-only | resolve instructions and templates from the selected external resource package; available since 0.21.0 and in the selected released 0.22.1 evaluator |\\n| `doctor` | human or agent | read-only | inspect installation integrity, required supplied files and evaluator identity |\\n| `preflight` | coding agent or reviewer | read-only | check one work order for start or review readiness and return its reading manifest |\\n| `evidence` | coding agent at a checkpoint | writes or rebinds one evidence packet header | write the work order's evidence packet with a machine header bound to the current formal snapshot, keeping the owner-authored body byte for byte |\\n| `pr-body` | coding agent opening a pull request | read-only | emit the LF-terminated pull-request body: the work-order line, the restitution line when a Git-derived handoff result is retained, and the evidence list; an unknown artifact is a failed result on standard output, exit 1, as for `check` and `evidence` |\\n| `check-pr` | managed GitHub CI | scope check; may rebind an in-progress handoff | check one or several approved work orders and their combined diff |\\n| `check` | human or agent selecting work or assessing a checkpoint | read-only, except the self-binding Git-derived handoff checkpoint, which rebinds the packet header and retains its completed result | without a checkpoint, return the selected artifact's complete execution context: state, governing chain, declared scope, reading manifest, next command and required decision, in one schema-2 result, selecting the single in_progress work order when none is named; with a checkpoint, evaluate one fixed checkpoint and emit canonical restitution |\\n| `transition` | authorized actor; a person or agent uses the same recorded WO approval for start and completion after local checks pass (see [one execution route](delegation-class.md)) | plan is read-only; `--apply` atomically mutates only explicitly selected artifacts | validate and record accountable lifecycle decisions without implicit related-record changes |\\n| `decide` | the human who holds `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`, directly or under an explicitly named eligible owner label | plan is read-only; `--apply` writes the decision's `[disposition]` table and one lifecycle event, and moves every raised risk the decision concerns in the same act | answer, defer, or withdraw one open decision artifact so the artifacts it blocks can move again |\\n| `raise-risk` | anyone working: a reviewer, an implementer, or an agent mid-execution; no decision right is needed | writes one risk artifact in `raised`, and with `--with-decision` the open decision that blocks the threatened artifacts; dry-run is read-only | record one measured threat to governed work so that an owner answers it before the threatened stage moves |\\n| `risks` | human or agent | read-only | list the risks threatening one artifact and its governing chain, with score, state and pending decision |\\n| `select-work-order` | managed GitHub CI | read-only | select exactly one standalone work-order declaration from a bounded pull-request event through released package logic |\\n| `upgrade` | repository owner or explicitly authorized agent | plan is read-only; apply replaces disposable copies and saves the provider last | select plugin skills or restore repository skills; rerun after an interruption |\\n| `scaffold-domain` | coding agent | writes owner-controlled directories and a seed index; dry-run is read-only | create the canonical organization for one engineering domain |\\n| `create-artifact` | coding agent | writes one incomplete `draft`; dry-run is read-only | create a formal artifact from its canonical template and path mapping |\\n| `release-unit` | release owner or coding agent drafting a release contract | read-only | measure a release unit's work-order census from the commit trailers between the previous release tag and a candidate commit, and compare it with a contract (`E-CIP-001`) |\\n| `identity` | CI or advanced contributor | read-only identity report/check | prove released-evaluator, candidate-source, or candidate-package runtime origin and boundary |\\n| `qualify` | release CI, maintainer, or released evaluator | read-only except for one exclusive evidence output outside the inspected repository | run one of four fixed evaluator/target qualification roles and emit provenance-bound, non-authoritative evidence |\\n| `capture-verification` | coding agent after an authorized clean candidate | writes one `ready` VREC plus canonical evaluator evidence | bind selected work, verification contracts, evidence, evaluator identity, snapshot, and exact clean `HEAD` |\\n| `refresh-verification` | coding agent after an unchanged rebase | writes a new `ready` VREC | compare relevant Git entries and reuse evidence while preserving the original |\\n| `prepare-release` | coding agent after verification and release-preparation authority | writes one `ready` RLS plus canonical evaluator evidence | bind release policy, eligible VRECs, exact work coverage, released evaluator wheel identity, version, and the same candidate commit |\\n\\n## Hosted sandbox client (unpublished)\\n\\n`harnessctl remote` is available in candidate client 0.22.2, installed into a\\nseparate test environment. The selected released evaluator 0.22.1 does not\\nprovide this command. Keep the released evaluator selected for repository and server checks.\\n\\nIn these examples, `CLIENT_PYTHON` is the absolute Python path in the separate\\ncandidate environment. Run from outside the checkout. `HAG_TEST_TOKEN` is the\\nname of a private environment variable; do not put its value in the command.\\n\\n```text\\n\\\"CLIENT_PYTHON\\\" -I -m se_harness remote status --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:18080 --token-env HAG_TEST_TOKEN --json\\n\\\"CLIENT_PYTHON\\\" -I -m se_harness remote read --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:18080 --token-env HAG_TEST_TOKEN --project PROJECT_ID --baseline BASELINE_ID --request READ_REQUEST_JSON --json\\n```\\n\\nThe positional argument is an operation, not a repository path. Every operation\\nrequires an explicit endpoint and credential-variable name. Operations other\\nthan `status` also require `--project`. `baseline` selects `--baseline`;\\n`operation` selects the original operation `--key`. `read`, `check`, and `query`\\nuse a versioned `--request` and an explicit baseline or context view.\\n\\nThe write operations are `import`, `draft-open`, `create-artifact`,\\n`revise-artifact`, and `freeze`. Each requires the complete versioned request\\nand `--client-wheel` identifying the actual separately installed candidate.\\nThere is no automatic retry, rebase, local fallback, or implicit apply step.\\nAfter an uncertain write, inspect its original operation key before retrying.\\n\\nThis client prints the remote protocol result, not the local evaluator result\\nschema. Transport errors go to standard error; an unknown write outcome is not\\na refusal or proof that nothing changed. See the [hosted sandbox guide](hosted-artifact-graph.md)\\nfor the request contracts and qualification limits. These commands do not\\napprove work, accept verification, or release artifacts.\\n\\n## Repository setup and inspection\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl init [TARGET] [--project-name NAME] [--integration git|ci|pr] [--dry-run] [--json]\\nharnessctl validate [TARGET] [--json] [--advisories]\\nharnessctl inspect [TARGET] [--json] [--vocabulary-threshold N]\\nharnessctl dashboard [TARGET] [--output PATH] [--json]\\nharnessctl doctor [TARGET] [--json]\\n```\\n\\n`TARGET` defaults to the current directory. The successor candidate defaults to\\nthe two selection files, with no copied instructions, templates or adoption report.\\nRepeat `--integration` for explicit Git evidence attributes, CI/output ignores,\\nor a PR template. Installation resolves every destination before writing and\\nrefuses conflicts and linked or escaping paths. Published 0.20.0 retains its\\nrepository-copy behavior; these candidate options do not adopt a release.\\n\\nValidation reports deterministic errors and warnings but does not edit artifacts. Each finding names its assessment plane: `structure`, `governance`, configured `policy`, or non-blocking `maintenance`. Planes explain the finding source; they do not change severity, pass/fail behavior, or create a score.\\n\\nThe summary line carries a fourth number, `Advisories`. An advisory is a hint for the author of a draft requirement or intent (the `W-AUT-*` codes: statement shape, one obligation, length and budgets, the old free-text `verification_method`, the intent's outcome and success measures). It is not a warning: it is raised only while the artifact is `draft`, it is left out of the warning count and the plane counts, and it is listed only with `--advisories`. The JSON report always carries `advisories` and `advisory_count`. On a repository whose definitions are all approved, `Advisories: 0` is the normal reading. Since 0.18.0 the approval transition of a draft intent, capability, requirement or specification is refused while any advisory remains on it (`QGP-G1-AUTHORING`, `QGP-G2-AUTHORING`, `SPEC-TCM-007`); the refusal names each advisory and ends with `fix the draft and run the transition again`. `validate` itself keeps passing.\\n\\nInspection reuses the existing validator and Harness Explorer snapshot. It\\nreports `mode = repository_wide`, no selected artifact, formal validity, ready\\ndecisions, draft definitions, active work, assurance preparation, and existing\\nrepository findings. Human output groups repeated rule instances for\\nreadability; `--json` retains every finding. Inspection output MUST NOT be used\\nas selected-iteration restitution.\\n\\nThe `assurance_pending` queue contains only an `implemented` work order whose explicit `[assurance]` classification is `required` and which has no direct `ready`, `verified`, or `released` VREC coverage. It suggests non-automatic preparation after one clean candidate commit; it does not select aggregate scope, create a record, or make the assurance decision. Completed legacy work without a classification and work explicitly classified `not_required` are not inferred into this queue.\\n\\nThe temporal reassessment observation `W-HEX-003` is deliberately narrow: it compares dates only for supported declared dependency relations whose source can still be meaningfully reassessed. It does not reopen completed work orders, reinterpret commit-bound verification or release records, or treat derived graph projections as declared dependencies.\\n\\nFor existing lifecycle queues and a closed set of actionable derived warning rules, inspection also reports deterministic suggested next steps. Each suggestion identifies its source, affected artifacts, action class, accountable role, and `automatic = false`. Suggestions contain no executable command and never assert eligibility or authority. Validator findings, informational observations, and unknown rules remain visible without guessed advice.\\n\\nInspection ends with a vocabulary section. It counts the words of every artifact's statement and body with code removed, drops common English and the harness terms the managed instructions define, and names the project terms at or above `--vocabulary-threshold` occurrences (default 50, between 30 and 100) that have no entry in `GLOSSARY.md` at the repository root, and the entries whose term appears in no artifact. The glossary is repository content. Published repository-copy installations seed it empty; minimal external-resource installation creates no glossary. Both routes preserve an existing glossary. The section is informational and never blocks.\\n\\nA successfully produced inspection exits zero even when formal validation failed or attention exists, so use `validate` when gate exit behavior is required. Inspection is repository-local derived evidence: it does not approve, authorize, verify, supersede, release, remediate, or independently govern the repository.\\n\\nDashboard defaults to `target/harness-dashboard/`; its generated files are derived evidence, not formal authority. The small `index.html` bootstrap verifies `dashboard-manifest.json`, then loads a summary, compact topology, readiness data, individual artifact details, and explicitly expanded evidence from digest-named static resources. Serve the directory from one HTTP origin, for example with `python -m http.server 8000 --directory target/harness-dashboard`; direct `file://` opening is intentionally rejected because progressive resource loading and integrity checks require an origin. Generation remains local and needs no application server, but publishing or sharing the directory exposes every manifest-declared artifact and evidence body; the command does not scan for secrets or redact repository material. Doctor checks the standard installed contract against `.engineering-harness.lock` and the current distribution.\\n\\n## Standalone draft validation\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate-draft [TARGET] --artifact ARTIFACT-ID [--json]\\n```\\n\\nThe caller supplies a complete projection. The command uses one parsed catalog\\nand the executing evaluator's canonical templates. It writes nothing. JSON is\\n`se-harness-draft-validation-v1`, with `selection` (id, type, status, relative\\npath), `admissible`, `errors`, `incomplete`, and `background`. Findings include\\nstable codes and structured field/relation/target details where relevant.\\nText reports the same facts. Exit 0 means admissible; 1 means a produced refusal;\\n2 means usage or a failure before a result can be produced.\\n\\nSupported draft types: intent, capability, requirement, specification,\\narchitecture, adr, verification, work_order, release_contract and\\noperating_contract. Decision, risk, verification_record and release_record\\ncontinue through their existing commands.\\n\\nA requirement with `CAP-xxx`, an omitted `derives_from`, or an empty array can\\nbe admissible with an incomplete finding. A link to an existing release record,\\nan unknown non-template target, or `[\\\"CAP-xxx\\\", \\\"RLS-SEH-001\\\"]` is refused.\\nMalformed TOML and duplicate IDs block a trustworthy catalog globally. Other\\nunselected findings remain background. A correct endpoint does not establish\\nreadiness of its full governing chain.\\n\\nSelection outside draft, lifecycle history and disposition are refused. This\\nsnapshot query cannot prove that imported identity or provenance is unchanged.\\nThe hosted caller must compare protected fields to its immutable base and enforce\\nrights and expected versions. Admission does not waive validation, approval,\\nverification or release gates, and includes no lifecycle next step.\\n\\n<a id=\\\"released-resource-lookup-successor-candidate\\\"></a>\\n\\n## Released resource lookup\\n\\nReleased evaluators since 0.21.0 provide this command for repositories selecting\\nthe `released-resources-v1` layout. This repository uses independently installed\\n0.22.1 after explicit adoption under WO-HUP-030. Publication alone does not\\nchange a repository's selection.\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl resources [TARGET] [--resource RESOURCE-ID] [--content] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nWithout `--resource`, list resource IDs, local paths, byte digests and headings\\nfrom the exact selected release. Use a returned ID with `--resource` to select\\none item. `--content` requires that one ID; it does not return every guide at\\nonce. For `ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md`, it renders the project and selected version\\nin memory. No instruction copy or lifecycle state is written to the repository.\\n\\nJSON output uses `se-harness-resources-v1`, with the selected `release` identity\\nand `resources` array. Content requests also return `content` and\\n`content_sha256`. Missing, altered or mismatched selected resources cause a\\nrefusal; the command does not install resources or borrow another release.\\n\\n## Work readiness\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight [TARGET] --work-order WO-... [--phase start|review] [--json]\\nharnessctl select-work-order --event GITHUB_EVENT_PATH [--json]\\n```\\n\\n`start` is the default phase. Preflight checks lifecycle eligibility, the governing chain, and the selected work order's explicit `[assurance]` declaration, then displays the classification, rationale, and deciding role with the reading manifest. A selected work order without a valid declaration fails even when completed legacy validation remains compatible. Passing proves structural readiness only; it does not prove comprehension, semantic scope fit, implementation correctness, the truth of the rationale or role claim, assurance, or release.\\n\\n`select-work-order` reads one bounded event file. A body uses either\\n`Harness-Work-Order: WO-AAA-001` or\\n`Harness-Work-Orders: WO-AAA-001, WO-BBB-002`. Use `--field work-orders`\\nfor one ID per output line. LF and CRLF are equivalent. Both declarations\\ntogether, duplicate IDs and malformed IDs are rejected.\\n\\n```sh\\nharnessctl check-pr [TARGET] --event EVENT.json --from-git BASE [--json]\\n```\\n\\n`check-pr` evaluates every selected approved work order and the complete diff\\nagainst their combined scope. Unrelated changes are not admitted by listing\\nanother work order; that work order must actually cover the path. In-progress\\nwork also needs passing local handoff checks. CI calls this command directly.\\n\\n\\n## Selected-scope workflow execution\\n\\nThe command shapes below are stable interfaces. The candidate standard\\n[`CONTINUE.md`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md#continue-selected-work)\\nroutes to the selected procedure, and\\n[`WORKFLOW.json`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/WORKFLOW.json)\\nis the machine-readable contract loaded by `harnessctl`. Use the workflow rule\\nselected for the artifact's exact type, state, and direct related records. Do\\nnot derive a new transition or next action from this reference.\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl evidence [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff \\\\\\n  [--rebound-at RFC3339] [--json]\\nharnessctl pr-body [TARGET] --artifact WO-... [--json]\\nharnessctl check [TARGET] [--artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-...] [--json] [--include-background]  # without a checkpoint: the projection\\nharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --planned-path PATH [--planned-path PATH ...] [--json]\\nharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-... \\\\\\n  --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff|scope [--target STATE] \\\\  # with a checkpoint:\\n  [--procedure PROC-...] [--from-git BASE | --changed-path PATH ... \\\\\\n  [--changes-complete] | --change-manifest PATH] [--pull-request-body PATH] [--json]\\nharnessctl transition [TARGET] --set ID=STATUS --decision ID=ACTOR \\\\\\n  [--set ID=STATUS ...] [--decision ID=ACTOR ...] [--reason ID=TEXT ...] \\\\\\n  [--apply] [--json]\\n```\\n\\n`check` without `--checkpoint` is the one call an agent makes first (`WO-ECP-001`,\\nfolded from `next` by `WO-ECP-019`). It returns the projection of the selected artifact \\u2014 the single\\n`in_progress` work order when `--artifact` is absent, otherwise `WEX-ECP-001` names the candidate\\ncount \\u2014 with an additive `context` object: `reading_manifest` (the preflight manifest for the\\nphase the state implies, `start` for `approved` and `in_progress`, `review` afterwards),\\n`governing`, `declared_paths`, `state`, `next` (`argv`, `procedure_id`, `step_id`, the same step a\\ncheckpoint `check` selects) and `decision_required`. It writes nothing and needs no prior command.\\nThe human block renders the context as a `Context` section after `Command or response`, and\\n`result_sha256` binds it. The former `next` command was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-020`); its\\ntombstone guard left with 0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown.\\n\\n`check` without `--checkpoint` projects only the selected artifact's governing chain and direct\\nlifecycle dependencies. It uses the ordered recommendation registry in\\n`WORKFLOW.json`. For example, `WFL-WO-READY-VREC` takes precedence over\\n`WFL-WO-PREPARE-VREC`, so existing ready assurance coverage cannot produce a\\nduplicate-capture recommendation. Unrelated repository findings remain a\\nbackground count; `--include-background` expands categories without making\\nthem selected-scope work.\\n\\nThe optional `--planned-path` view assesses proposed files before approval.\\nIt requires an explicit work order and no checkpoint. Repeat the option for\\neach repository-relative file in the plan; the file need not exist yet.\\nExisting calls without this option are unchanged.\\n\\nThe schema-2 result adds `scope.preparation`: `planned_paths`, `coverage`\\n(`covered`, `uncovered` or `invalid`), `explicit_matches` with the matching\\n`scope_entry`, `automatic_matches` with the existing admission rule,\\n`uncovered_paths`, `invalid_declarations` and\\n`impact_analysis: \\\"not_assessed\\\"`. These machine fields participate in the\\nresult digest. The human report lists coverage and each path's reason.\\n\\nThe normal lifecycle projection, next action, exit meaning and gate fields\\nare preserved. **Exit zero does not mean the plan is covered.** Inspect\\n`scope.preparation.coverage` and resolve uncovered or invalid paths before\\nrequesting approval. Coverage cannot prove that the agent found every\\naffected file. Planning writes nothing and does not populate actual changed\\npaths, assert completeness, evaluate gates or authorize work.\\n\\nThe selected WO file and existing directly linked VREC/RLS records and their\\ndeclared evaluator evidence use their existing exact-path admission rules.\\nThe selected WO's own packet directory is reported separately under its\\nexisting admission rule.\\nAn unallocated future record has no assessable path; explain its expected\\nrelationship rule and check the actual destination after preparation.\\nOther review/log evidence needs explicit scope unless an existing rule covers\\nit. A neighboring file is not admitted by a generated record's directory.\\n\\nDo not combine planned paths with `--checkpoint`, `--target`, `--procedure`,\\n`--changed-path`, `--changes-complete`, `--change-manifest`, `--from-git`\\nor `--pull-request-body`. Invalid selection, malformed paths, case duplicates,\\ndirectory inputs and repository escapes are refused through normal diagnostics.\\nThis option must be used with a released evaluator that provides it; candidate\\nsource tests do not change the repository's selected evaluator.\\n\\nWith a checkpoint, `check` resolves the first matching rule, its typed `PROC-*` procedure, and its\\n`QG-*` gates; `--checkpoint scope` evaluates only the scope predicates of\\n`QG-G4-IMPLEMENTATION-EVIDENCE` for a work order in any lifecycle state and\\nwrites nothing, which is what the managed pull-request gate runs (`WO-ECP-013`); [`harnessctl check` explained](harnessctl-check.md) walks\\nthrough the checkpoints, the rule table, the gates, and the refusal codes. `--checkpoint transition --target STATE` previews, read-only, the\\nexact predicates and graph-structural checks `transition --set ID=STATE` will\\nevaluate (`WO-ECP-009`): the transition binding index of `QUALITY_GATES.json`\\nkeyed by artifact family and target state, evaluated by the same gate evaluator\\nwith the same context, plus the `QGS-*` checks under the synthetic\\n`QG-STRUCTURAL` gate. A transition whose evaluation is not all `pass` renders\\n`Blocked by` with each refusing predicate's own identifier and writes nothing;\\nan applied transition that would be blocked fails closed with that identifier. `pre-action` requires `--procedure`, which must equal the selected\\nprocedure or one complete declared alternative. `--changed-path` may repeat;\\n`--changes-complete` asserts that the supplied set is complete, including an\\nempty set. The assertion is evidence, not proof from a trusted Git baseline.\\nWithout it, path-scope predicates are `not_assessable`.\\n\\n`--from-git BASE` derives the change set from Git instead of from typed\\npaths: the union of `git diff --name-only BASE` against the working tree\\n(renames contribute both names) and the untracked files Git does not ignore,\\neach normalized as above; the set is complete by construction and the result\\nrecords `change_set_source = \\\"git\\\"`. It is mutually exclusive with the\\nchanged-path options and the manifest (`WEX-ECP-002`); outside a Git\\ncheckout, with a base Git cannot resolve, or on any Git failure it blocks\\nwith `WEX-ECP-003` and evaluates no predicate as `pass`. The selected work\\norder's own artifact file, written by its lifecycle transitions and so always\\nin the diff, is admitted to its scope by construction (`ECP-CHG-007`).\\n\\n`evidence` writes `DOMAIN/evidence/WO-ID/WO-ID-CHECKPOINT.md` (`WO-ECP-002`):\\na fenced TOML header at byte offset 0 with exactly `artifact`, `checkpoint`,\\n`formal_snapshot_sha256` and `rebound_at`, followed by an owner-authored\\nbody. On an existing packet only the header bytes change; the body is\\nretained byte for byte, and a file without a header at offset 0, with a\\nheader naming another artifact or checkpoint, or with invalid TOML is refused\\n(`WEX-ECP-010`). It refuses when a `.gitattributes` rule would convert the\\npacket's line endings (`WEX-ECP-011`) and when the single `in_progress` work\\norder is not the one named (`WEX-ECP-012`). `QGP-G4I-EVIDENCE` reads that\\nheader through a TOML parser; a packet without one is not assessable, and\\nthe message names the `evidence` command that writes the header (the\\none-release substring grace closed under `WO-AUT-006`). `check --checkpoint handoff\\n--from-git BASE` is self-binding (`ECP-SBH-001` to `-006`): it rebinds an\\nexisting packet header to the current formal snapshot before evaluating \\u2014\\nbody preserved, `evidence`'s `WEX-ECP-010`/`WEX-ECP-011` guards unchanged,\\nno packet created \\u2014 and evaluates the change set with the retained result\\npath included, so one run is the declared, digest-stable result. A\\ncompleted run retains its schema-2 result as `handoff.json` in the same\\ndirectory, written by the harness; that directory is admitted to the work\\norder's scope by construction.\\n\\n`pr-body` emits the pull-request body for an approved or later work order\\n(`WEX-ECP-014` otherwise): the standalone `Harness-Work-Order` line first, one\\nstandalone `Harness-Restitution` line carrying the retained `handoff.json`'s\\n`result_sha256` when it exists, then the seeded `## Summary` and\\n`## Verification` headings with every evidence path under the packet\\ndirectory. LF line endings only; the body round-trips through\\n`select-work-order` unchanged, so paste its output rather than typing it.\\n\\n`--change-manifest` is mutually exclusive with both changed-path options. It\\nmust be an in-repository UTF-8 JSON object containing only `schema` with value\\n`se-harness-change-set-v1`, Boolean `complete`, and ordered array `paths`.\\nPaths use `/`, exact-file or component-boundary directory-prefix matching, and\\nreject absolute, traversal, backslash, wildcard, drive, URI, control-character,\\nreserved-device, duplicate, and case-ambiguous forms.\\n\\n`check` always emits `se-harness-workflow-result-v2`. That structured result is\\nauthoritative. The deterministic direct human renderer uses `Outcome`, `Done`,\\n`Not done`, conditional `Blocked by`, `Current lifecycle state`, `Decision\\nrequired`, `Next`, `Command or response`, and conditional `Alternatives` in\\nthat order. Exact-format consumers must use this renderer directly rather than\\nask a model to transcribe it. `check`, `transition`, `capture-verification`,\\nand `prepare-release` emit the same `se-harness-workflow-result-v2` result\\nthrough one selector (`WO-ECP-005`); the former `--result-schema` option is\\ngone and passing it is an argument error. Each rule in `WORKFLOW.json` carries\\nonly the `done` and `current_lifecycle_state` prose of its restitution; the\\nnext step and the command come from the bound procedure.\\n\\nWhen `check` is blocked, `Next` and `Command or response` carry the corrective\\nform the contract declares for the first failing predicate: a command that\\ndiffers from the evaluated one (for example the handoff check with\\n`--changed-path` and `--changes-complete`), an escalation naming a decision\\nright, or a response describing the evidence to retain. The evaluated command\\nis never rendered as its own retry. Every schema-2 result carries\\n`result_sha256`. New results declare `digest_format = \\\"machine-fields-v1\\\"`\\nand hash stable machine fields rather than human wording. Retained results\\nwithout the marker keep their original human-block digest; a pull-request body may declare it on one standalone\\n`Harness-Restitution:` line for CI to recompute. At `handoff`, a work order\\nwhose `ready` verification record binds a commit no longer reachable from\\n`HEAD` is blocked with `W-ADS-002`; `--pull-request-body` additionally reports\\n`W-ADS-001` when the work-order trailer ends with a carriage return.\\n\\nAn agent-facing handoff may adapt wording, ordering, headings, and relevant\\nexplanation or omit empty fields. It remains conforming only when it preserves\\nactual artifact IDs, outcome, observed effects, incomplete work, material\\nnon-effects, blockers, final lifecycle state, the accountable decision,\\ncommand argument boundaries or suggested-response meaning, and exactly one\\nrecommended next action. Workflow-declared alternatives remain separate from\\nthat recommendation. Agent prose never becomes lifecycle authority.\\n\\n`transition` resolves IDs from formal metadata and plans by default. Each\\nselected ID needs one actor assertion. Rejection needs a non-empty reason; VREC\\nsupersession uses the reason as the exact successor VREC ID. A packet is\\nassessed as one proposed final graph. `--apply` rechecks every input byte,\\nproves the locked released-evaluator authority before writing, stages\\nsame-filesystem replacements outside artifact discovery, and rolls back earlier\\nreplacements if a later write fails.\\n\\nThe command records actor text as an assertion, not proof of authority. The\\neffects and non-effects for each state are defined only by the matching\\n`WORKFLOW.json` rule. Related artifacts require separate explicit selection,\\npassing gates, and authority.\\n\\nDirect human and JSON output are rendered from the same semantic workflow\\nresult. Schema 2 always identifies exactly one typed next step and derives its\\ncommand argument array or response from the selected procedure. Adaptive agent\\npresentation consumes that result; it does not replace or recompute it.\\n\\n## Decision disposition\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--revisit TEXT] [--apply] [--json]\\nharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO ... --revisit TEXT --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\\nharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --withdraw --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\\n```\\n\\nA decision artifact (`DEC-`) records one pending question, or one implementation deviation from one rule of one specification. While it is `open`, every artifact named in its `blocks` relation is refused its transitions by the `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate of the gate that transition would pass. The refusal names the decision, its question, its options, the deciding role, and the `decide` command that clears it.\\n\\n`decide` is the only way a decision changes state; `transition` refuses it. Without `--apply` the command plans and reports; with `--apply` it writes the `[disposition]` table (the option, its label, the actual human, the time, and the verbatim reason) and one lifecycle event. `--option` must name one of the options the artifact declares. A deferral needs one `--scope` entry per transition it admits and a `--revisit` trigger; the scoped transitions pass, every other blocked transition still waits. Accepting a deviation needs `--revisit`, because acceptance is time-bounded. An ineligible owner is refused with `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`.\\n\\n`--decision ACTOR` records the actual human who made the decision. With\\n`--authority-owner OWNER`, the evaluator checks OWNER against the existing\\nholders for the blocked artifacts, or the departed specification for a\\ndeviation. OWNER must match exactly and contain non-blank printable text of\\nat most 128 characters. It is retained separately as `authority_owner` in\\nthe disposition. Without the option, ACTOR must directly match a holder.\\nBoth preview and apply use the same checks. The CLI does not authenticate\\nthese claims or grant consent; the caller must first establish the human's\\nauthority and obtain the exact decision. Existing owner labels and historical\\nrecords are not changed.\\n\\nThe validator reports a malformed decision as `E-DCM-001` to `E-DCM-003`, prose in a legacy definition's `## Open decisions` section as `E-DCM-004`, a deviation whose `against` fragment is not a rule identifier of the named specification (`SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN`) as `E-DCM-005`, and an accepted deviation past its revisit or accepted twice against the same rule as `W-DCM-001` and `W-DCM-002`. See [decision artifacts](decision-artifacts.md) for the model.\\n\\nWhen the decision concerns a raised risk, `--apply` also moves that risk to the state the option names, in the same act: `accept` needs `--revisit`, `mitigate` needs `--mitigated-by WO-...`, and `avoid` records `--avoided-by` (an ADR or a decision; it defaults to the disposing decision). A deferral leaves the risk `raised`; a withdrawal withdraws it.\\n\\n## Risk recording\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk [TARGET] --domain SLUG --title TEXT --stage STAGE --category CATEGORY --cause TEXT --effect TEXT --likelihood N --impact N --threatens ID [--threatens ID ...] --raised-by ACTOR [--owner ROLE ...] [--id RISK-...] [--with-decision [--decision-id DEC-...] [--recommend accept|avoid|mitigate]] [--dry-run] [--json]\\nharnessctl risks [TARGET] --artifact ID [--json]\\n```\\n\\nA risk artifact (`RISK-`) records one measured threat: one cause, one effect, the stage it threatens, `likelihood` and `impact` from 1 to 5, and their product as `score`. `raise-risk` computes the score, writes the file in `raised` and records the raise as a lifecycle event, in one act; a measurement outside the range or an identifier already declared anywhere is refused before anything is written, exit 2. `--domain` takes the domain slug or the identifier token of exactly one domain. With `--with-decision` the command also writes the open decision that blocks the threatened artifacts, with the options `accept`, `avoid` and `mitigate`. No gate reads risks: the stop is the paired decision's `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate, and the refusal names the decision, not the risk.\\n\\n`risks` lists every risk threatening the named artifact or, for a work order, its governing chain; it writes nothing.\\n\\nThe validator reports a missing or invalid field as `E-RSK-001`, a wrong measurement or score as `E-RSK-002`, a raised risk that no pending decision names as `E-RSK-003`, a paired decision whose `blocks` differs from the risk's `threatens` as `E-RSK-004`, a disposition typed by hand as `E-RSK-005`, and an accepted risk past its revisit as `W-RSK-001`. See [risk artifacts](risk-artifacts.md) for the model.\\n\\n## Safe repository upgrade\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] [--json]\\nharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply [--json]\\nharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply --work-order WO-... --evidence-output docs/engineering/DOMAIN/evidence/WO-...-evaluator-upgrade.json [--json]\\n```\\n\\nThe first form is a read-only plan. `--apply` is an explicit transactional repository mutation. Same-identity managed repair needs no new lifecycle packet. When the installed target evaluator differs from the standard lock, apply additionally requires a distinct approved or in-progress work order with an exact `[evaluator_upgrade]` packet and a work-order-keyed JSON evidence path. The packet binds the prior lock SHA-256 and exact immutable target archive/payload identity with `scope = \\\"standard-root-only\\\"`; a product release decision cannot substitute for it.\\n\\nApply requires the already-published target evaluator installed from exact wheel bytes outside the checkout, changes only eligible managed content, and stops without a partial managed update when identity, authority, customization, or conflict prevents a safe plan. Transition evidence, managed files, and the lock share the recoverable transaction, and successful replay must be a no-op. Every repository, including the `se_harness` implementation repository, follows this transaction and uses one exact released evaluator. GitHub discovers the managed workflow beside existing repository-owned workflows, while required-check and workflow-ordering policy remains external. See [installation and safe upgrades](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md).\\n\\n## Retained skill ownership\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider plugin --plugin-root DIRECTORY [--apply] [--json]\\nharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider repository [--apply] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nThis candidate command is unavailable in released 0.17.0. It removes the two\\nnamed harness skill directories under .agents/skills and .claude/skills,\\nincluding edits and extra files. Other skill directories remain unchanged.\\nThe replacement must contain a Verity Plane manifest and the six required files.\\nPreview is optional. Apply reads current inputs, deletes the old copies, and\\nsaves the portable provider choice last. Rerun the command after an interruption.\\nRestoration copies the current repository templates over disposable old copies.\\nThis file-only operation grants no lifecycle authority and does not install a\\nplugin or change host settings. See [the current design](plugin-simplification-2026-09-13.md).\\n\\n## Predecessor-to-successor migration rehearsal\\n\\nThe former `rehearse-recovery` command is retired (`WO-ECP-030`, issue #376; it had no workflow caller and no retained report), as the former `rehearse-migration` command was (`WO-ECP-010`, issue #210); the root-evaluator handover is rehearsed by `python -m repository_tools.upgrade_rehearsal`, a repository-owned tool described in [rehearsing the root-evaluator handover](evaluator-migration-rehearsal.md), not by a `harnessctl` subcommand.\\n\\n\\n## Domain and artifact authoring\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN [--title TITLE] [--dry-run] [--json]\\nharnessctl create-artifact [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE [--id ID] [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nDomain slugs, artifact identifiers, type prefixes, templates, and destinations are validated before mutation. `create-artifact` creates only an incomplete `draft`; it does not choose owners, relations, content, approval, or authority. After creation it prints the created type's checklist from `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`, resolved in the selected wheel for the external layout or in the repository for a supported older layout; `--quiet` suppresses it. Existing valid flat layouts remain discoverable and are not automatically migrated.\\n\\nWithout `--id`, `create-artifact` allocates the lowest free\\n`TYPE-DOMAIN-NNN` across every local branch and tag and the working tree,\\nuntracked files included (`WO-ECP-002`): the refs are enumerated with\\n`git for-each-ref` and each ref's `docs/engineering` tree is listed, so two\\nagents on two branches cannot take the same number; remote-tracking refs are\\nnot consulted. The domain token is read from the domain's existing\\nartifacts. The result names the refs on which the next-lower identifier was\\nfound, so a gap is explained. Outside a Git checkout allocation is refused\\n(`WEX-ECP-013`) rather than guessed from the working tree. An explicit `--id`\\nis refused when any local ref already carries it.\\n\\nNon-dry-run authoring uses the common pre-write mutation guard. The invoking environment must match the schema-3 released-evaluator identity locked by the target repository; candidate source and editable or contaminated installs fail without creating the requested path.\\n\\n## Release unit derivation\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl release-unit [TARGET] --from TAG --to COMMIT [--exempt SHA ...] [--contract REL-ID] [--json | --toml]\\n```\\n\\nMeasures the work-order trailers between the previous release tag and a\\ncandidate commit, including merged work. The JSON shape remains compatible.\\nUntraced commits, incomplete census information, and contract differences are\\nadvisory and exit successfully; invalid Git refs or command inputs still fail.\\n`--exempt` remains readable for old invocations but is unnecessary. The owner\\napproves final release scope, and the final candidate still needs verification.\\n\\n## Runtime identity\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl identity --role released-evaluator|candidate-source|candidate-package \\\\\\n  --expected-version VERSION --expected-root PATH [options] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nKey role-specific options are `--checkout-root`, `--candidate-commit`, `--evaluator-wheel-sha256`, `--entry-point`, `--require-isolated-python`, and `--require-entry-point`. The command verifies declared runtime origin; it does not select an evaluator or approve a candidate.\\n\\nRuntime identity also observes the running interpreter's own entry-point path through the declared interpreter-safety rule and records three additional facts: whether the entry point is a symbolic link, which position class its resolved target occupies relative to the expected and checkout roots, and the target's SHA-256. The schema identifier stays `se-harness-runtime-identity-v3`, because consumers require a subset of the identity rather than an exact field set. The observation is recorded for every role, but only the two environment-bounded roles \\u2014 `released-evaluator` and `candidate-package` \\u2014 turn a refusal into the `RID024` diagnostic; `candidate-source` has no environment boundary, because its expected root is the checkout itself. `RID004` and `RID006` keep their existing meanings unchanged.\\n\\n## Role-specific release qualification\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl qualify released-root [ROOT] [--output PATH] [--json]\\nharnessctl qualify complete-candidate [ROOT] --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT [--output PATH] [--json]\\nharnessctl qualify candidate-package --candidate-wheel PATH --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT --candidate-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --verifier-wheel-sha256 SHA256 [--checkout-root PATH] [--output PATH] [--json]\\nharnessctl qualify public-install [ROOT] --release-record RLS-... --public-wheel PATH --public-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --payload-sha256 SHA256 [--output PATH] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nThe four subcommands are separate closed parsers. They bind evaluator identity, target identity, fixed checks, and one independence class before reporting a result. They do not accept a general evaluator, validator, script, omission, or diagnostic-allowlist option. `--output` must name a new external file; the command never overwrites it or writes qualification evidence inside the inspected repository.\\n\\n`--evaluator-python` is judged by the declared interpreter-safety rule before anything is spawned. Supply the environment's own lexical entry point \\u2014 `bin/python` on POSIX, `Scripts/python.exe` on Windows \\u2014 not the resolved system interpreter it points at. The environment root is derived from that lexical path, so an interpreter reached through a linked or junctioned parent directory is refused, as is one inside the inspected checkout or whose resolved target lands inside it. The terminal interpreter link itself is permitted, which is what makes an ordinary `python -m venv` environment usable on POSIX.\\n\\nAll operations emit `se-harness-release-qualification-v1`. The result identifies the operation, completion, outcome, evaluator, target, ordered checks, independence boundary, and its evidence-only authority. `complete-candidate` is always `candidate-controlled`, even when it passes. See [release qualification roles](release-qualification-roles.md) for the workflow map. `WO-REB-028` retired a fifth operation, `predecessor-view`, with the predecessor-bootstrap release path; its `PV001` and `PV002` codes stay reserved and no code path emits them.\\n\\nThe pre-namespace `accept-candidate` entry point, kept as a one-cycle alias of `qualify\\ncandidate-package` under `REQ-REB-022`, was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-019`); its tombstone guard left with\\n0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown. Exact public 0.6.0 predates the `qualify` namespace;\\nits immutable command still emits `se-harness-functional-acceptance-v1` and is accepted only as\\nexplicitly labeled bootstrap evidence in the candidate workflow's legacy branch, which runs only a\\nverifier without `qualify`. That historical output is not converted into or described as canonical\\nqualification evidence.\\n\\n## Commit-bound verification preparation\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification [TARGET] \\\\\\n  --id VREC-... \\\\\\n  --work-order WO-... \\\\\\n  --verification VER-... \\\\\\n  --evidence PATH \\\\\\n  [--owner ROLE] [--domain DOMAIN] [--output PATH] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nRefusals distinguish invalid state (`WEX301`), Git provenance (`WEX302`),\\nevidence (`WEX303`), and record inputs (`WEX304`). Repeat work orders, contracts,\\nand evidence paths for a final aggregate candidate. Work may be implemented,\\nverified, or released; all declared verification contracts must be selected.\\nEvidence may be a shared integration report plus earlier verification records.\\nThe command writes a ready VREC and evaluator evidence. It does not verify it.\\n\\nAfter WO-KIS-009, each selected WO's recorded execution approval and unchanged\\nscope authorize preparation for either a person or an agent. There is no\\nactor-specific single-WO limit. Use the installed evaluator's procedure on a\\nrepository still governed by an earlier release until normal upgrade.\\nUse `--candidate-commit COMMIT --test-command <argv...>` to test the exact final\\nintegration in a temporary checkout, including when the caller has local edits.\\n\\nFor a harmless rebase, use\\n`harnessctl refresh-verification REPO --from VREC-OLD-001 --id VREC-NEW-001`.\\nThis compares relevant Git tree entries, governing inputs, and retained evidence.\\nIt preserves the old ready record and writes a new ready successor. Changed\\nrelevant files require fresh tests; verified records cannot be refreshed.\\n\\nAn accountable assurance owner reviews the retained evidence and separately decides whether to transition the VREC to `verified`. The record lives in later governance history and continues to bind the earlier candidate commit C.\\n\\nIf a later verified or released VREC fully covers a prepared ready record, the assurance owner may instead apply the declared `ready -> superseded` transition and name that successor with `--reason`. The command preserves `prepared_at` and `prepared_by`, adds only the supersession decision fields, typed successor relation, lifecycle event, status, and update date, and does not add `verified_at` or `verified_by`. Supersession means the proposal was retired, not verified. Historical superseded VRECs without preparation fields may retain the older valid `verified_at` capture shape; validation does not rewrite them or fabricate `verified_by`.\\n\\n## Commit-bound release preparation\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release [TARGET] \\\\\\n  --id RLS-... \\\\\\n  --release-contract REL-... \\\\\\n  --verification-record VREC-... \\\\\\n  --work-order WO-... \\\\\\n  --version VERSION \\\\\\n  --owner ROLE \\\\\\n  [--tag TAG] [--domain DOMAIN] [--output PATH] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nThe corresponding release refusal codes are `WEX401` to `WEX404`. Select one\\nverified or released final-candidate VREC and repeat `--work-order` for the\\nrelease scope. The final record must cover exactly that work and all its\\nverification contracts. The RLS binds its exact candidate commit. Earlier\\nrecords may be cited as supporting evidence at different commits; passing\\ntheir individual checks cannot replace final integration verification.\\n\\nBefore writing, the command proves the locked released evaluator including its wheel filename and SHA-256. It writes canonical normalized evaluator evidence and binds the evidence path and digest in the `status = \\\"ready\\\"` RLS. The record contains `prepared_at` and `prepared_by`; it omits `released_at` and `authorized_by` until a separate release transition. For the external layout, explicitly select `--integration git` or establish an equivalent owner rule before evidence writes. The selected `.gitattributes` fragment applies exactly `docs/engineering/**/evidence/*.json text eol=lf`, preserving canonical evidence bytes across supported checkouts so the raw SHA-256 survives. Independent validation and publication replay reject missing, changed, noncanonical, candidate-role, host-path-leaking, or lock-mismatched evidence. A rejected contract can support only its exact rejected RLS as terminal history and remains invalid for preparation, binding, release, publication, or credential-bearing use. The command does not transition the record to `released`, commit, push, tag, create a GitHub Release, publish to PyPI, or deploy.\\n\\nOnly `ready` and `released` release records claim a version. Valid rejected records remain immutable audit history and do not prevent one correctly bound active successor for an unpublished version; a second active record still fails.\\n\\n`WO-REB-028` retired the repository-specific schema-2 bootstrap path that once worked around released 0.5.0's inability to parse a rejected record: the predecessor preparation, assessment and publication-view adapters, their entry-point scripts, and the `qualify predecessor-view` operation are gone. Generic `harnessctl prepare-release` was never altered by that path and is unchanged by its removal. The retained 0.6.0 records keep their bytes and their hash-bound evidence digests; they are verifiable and no longer re-derivable. The real upgrade rehearsal, `python -m repository_tools.upgrade_rehearsal` (see [rehearsing the root-evaluator handover](evaluator-migration-rehearsal.md)), is the one mechanism for predecessor-to-successor assurance.\\n\\n## Authority summary\\n\\n| Result | Meaning |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| successful check | derived observation about the inspected repository or runtime |\\n| generated dashboard | derived navigation and anomaly evidence |\\n| generated `draft` | incomplete authoring starting point |\\n| generated `ready` VREC/RLS | structurally prepared proposal awaiting accountable review |\\n| human transition to `verified` | assurance decision about the exact candidate and evidence |\\n| human transition to `released` | release authorization for that same candidate |\\n\\nFor lifecycle timing, see [operational phasing](harness-operational-phasing.md). For complete examples, see [practical SE Harness examples](harness-lineage-example.md).\\n\\n\\nTo capture while keeping local edits, add `--candidate-commit COMMIT` and put\\n`--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS...` last. Capture tests that commit in a\\ntemporary checkout and retains the command result in the record. A failed test\\nwrites no record; uncommitted caller content is not used as tested evidence.\\n\\n## Explicit resource migration (successor candidate)\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl upgrade TARGET --external-resources --prior-wheel PRIOR_WHEEL [--retire-file PATH] [--integration git|ci|pr] [--json]\\n```\\n\\nPreview first. Add `--apply` and `--instruction-delivery-evidence RECEIPT` to the\\nsame reviewed selection to retire its local entry. `--prior-wheel` must match\\nthe old selection; it is read as data to recognize stock bytes. Repeat\\n`--retire-file` only for explicitly selected unchanged editable seeds. Customized\\ninstruction seeds refuse migration. Historical and owner files stay intact.\\nSee the [migration procedure and resource map](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#migrate-a-repository-copy-installation).\\nOn an external-resource installation, `upgrade --integration git` previews the\\nGit attributes needed before hash-bound evidence. Repeat with `--apply` to write.\\n\\n## Editable files and lightweight identity (repository-copy layouts)\\n\\n`harnessctl upgrade TARGET --replace-file PATH` previews replacement of one\\neditable supplied file. Add `--apply` to write it; repeat the option for more\\nfiles. Other guidance, templates, CI and owner settings are kept. The selected\\nchecker version still has to match the installation record.\\n\\nOrdinary writes use checker origin/version. `doctor`, explicit `identity`,\\ninstallation, upgrade and release preparation check the full installed payload.\\nThe module route works without a console launcher. Runtime identity schema v4\\nreports Python version without hashing the executable. New evaluator evidence\\nschema v2 binds canonical validated values; legacy schema v1 remains readable.\\n\\n## Hosted lifecycle rehearsal (candidate client)\\n\\nThese commands belong to the separately installed candidate client. The selected\\nreleased evaluator remains 0.22.1 and is the service's sole lifecycle evaluator.\\n\\n```text\\nCLIENT_PYTHON -I -m se_harness remote rehearse --endpoint ENDPOINT --project PROJECT_ID --token-env TOKEN_VARIABLE --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --test-copy --request REQUEST_JSON --json\\nCLIENT_PYTHON -I -m se_harness remote operation --endpoint ENDPOINT --project PROJECT_ID --token-env TOKEN_VARIABLE --key ORIGINAL_KEY --json\\nCLIENT_PYTHON -I -m se_harness remote export --endpoint ENDPOINT --project PROJECT_ID --token-env TOKEN_VARIABLE --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --test-copy --request EXPORT_JSON --destination NEW_DIRECTORY --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the [closed v2 contract](../../server/contracts/lifecycle-v2.md) for request\\nfields, modes and allowed effects. `inspect` reports evaluator results. `preview`\\nstages a disposable result without changing graph state. `apply` requires the\\nreturned preview digest and unchanged inputs. Only `apply` creates an accepted\\noperation receipt. A retry with identical inputs returns that receipt; different\\ninputs under its key fail. No arbitrary command or `--test-command` is forwarded.\\n\\nExport requires an immutable baseline and a new directory. It writes exact files,\\na Git bundle and a manifest. Download success does not claim successful independent\\nreplay. All these records are test data; Git remains authoritative for real work.\\n\\n## Concise hosted authoring\\n\\nThe candidate client supports explicit typed inputs for existing operations.\\nThis does not change service schemas, select lifecycle actions or grant authority.\\nUse the installed candidate Python with `-I -m se_harness remote OPERATION`.\\nCommon selection is `--endpoint URL --project UUID --token-env VARIABLE`.\\nCredentials stay in that environment variable. The service remains a private\\nloopback sandbox; Git remains authoritative.\\n\\n| Operation | Required typed fields |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `remote import` | `--source-manifest FILE` |\\n| `remote draft-open` | `--baseline ID --work-order WO-ID` |\\n| `remote create-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --domain NAME --artifact-type TYPE`; optional `--artifact ID` |\\n| `remote revise-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --document-file FILE` |\\n| `remote read` (revision) | `--artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION` and exactly one of `--baseline ID` or `--context UUID --context-version N` |\\n\\nSelect `--typed`. Every mutation also requires `--operation-key KEY`,\\n`--expected-project-version N`, `--evaluator-file FILE`, and `--client-wheel FILE`.\\nThe evaluator file contains exactly `version`, `archive_sha256`, `payload_sha256`\\nfrom the selected combination. The client verifies the executing package against\\nits wheel. The source manifest uses the existing canonical manifest schema.\\nDocument files are exact UTF-8 bytes, at most 1 MiB. Linked paths are refused.\\nThe client constructs the existing wire request; the agent selects its meaning,\\nversions and key. It never retries or changes these inputs automatically.\\n\\nRaw `--request FILE` remains available for every existing operation, including\\nfreeze and test-copy lifecycle operations. Do not combine raw and typed input.\\nInvalid typed fields fail before a network request. Stale versions and reused\\nkeys with changed content retain the service's normal refusal behavior.\\n\\nAdd `--compact --record-directory NEW_DIRECTORY` for an evidence-backed view.\\nThe parent directory must exist; the destination must not exist or traverse a\\nlink. It retains exact request/response bytes, decoded documents and capture\\nmetadata (exit, timings, uncertainty). The view shows small fields and documents,\\nwith explicit pointers for omitted content. Required omitted findings still need\\nreading. It is a presentation, not an independent verdict.\\nFor known workflow results with a selected instruction step, the view can leave\\nthe full instruction-step catalogue and evaluator-only inputs in `full_response`\\nwhen their pointers are smaller. Their JSON pointers are listed in `omitted`.\\nThe response path is given once in `full_response`. The selected step, its\\nprerequisites, executable procedure, findings and next action stay in view.\\nFor draft-validation responses, `draft_review` identifies the evaluator's shape\\nand required-link checks and reports content review as `not_assessed`. An empty\\n`incomplete` list and `findings_complete: true` do not establish content readiness.\\nThe agent reviews the saved content against the applicable authoring checklist.\\n\\nFor `create-artifact`, optional `--include-document` performs one read of the\\nexact created revision after an accepted creation. No other mutation occurs.\\nIts `document_read` field retains the independent response. A failed read does\\nnot undo creation. After a capture or transport failure, inspect retained results\\nand look up the original operation key; a remote effect may have committed.\\nDo not choose a new key to conceal an unknown outcome. An explicit separate\\nrevision read remains available for verification.\\n\\n### Complete instruction sections\\n\\nFor a repository governed by a release that supports this option:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl resources REPO --section docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity --section docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#intent --json\\n```\\n\\nUse actual returned/selected headings. The example does not select a lifecycle\\nstep. `--section RESOURCE#heading` can repeat up to 12 times. Each complete section\\nincludes source path, selected release, digest and line range. Overlapping sections\\nare included once. The view also includes that file's **Read this when** and\\n**Before this action** sections when present and not already included. These\\nentry conditions retain their exact source bytes. The reader does not follow\\nlinks or choose a procedure; read applicable linked prerequisites separately.\\nUnknown or ambiguous headings and changed resources fail.\\nDo not mix `--section` with `--resource`/`--content`. Existing resource modes stay\\navailable. This candidate option does not make an older released evaluator support it.\\nThe native test adapter can use the same installed reader on byte-verified staged\\nreleased resources; that does not substitute candidate policy for the released evaluator.\\n\"}\r\n",

The displayed `client_view` is the\\nclient's own view. Inspect outcomes and findings; read required omitted content.\\nDo not reread a whole receipt just to extract a small field already displayed.\\nA capture error after send can leave a committed effect. Reconcile its original\\nkey with `remote operation --key KEY --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\n\\n## Read one revision\\n\\n```text\\nremote read --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --context UUID --context-version N\\n```\\n\\nFor an imported baseline, replace the context fields with `--baseline ID`.\\nReads take no `--operation-key`, `--expected-project-version` or `--evaluator-file`.\\nChoose the exact revision and context from the selected inputs or actual results.\\n\\n## Reads and discovery\\n\\n| Need | Operation |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Service readiness and selected components | `remote status --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` |\\n| Local wheel metadata | `identity` |\\n| Captured calls, reads and failures so far | `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`; retains the full snapshot and returns its field pointers, no content verdict |\\n| Complete released instruction sections | `instructions --section \\\"RESOURCE_ID#HEADING\\\"`; repeat for up to 12 sections |\\n| One unknown input location | `find-file BASENAME --under RELATIVE_DIRECTORY/` |\\n| One exact inventory entry | `lookup-file RELATIVE_NAME` |\\n| One saved JSON field | `read-json ABSOLUTE_FILE --pointer '\\\"/field\\\"'`; omit pointer for root; optional `--keys` |\\n| A raw base64 field | Add `--decode-base64` to that field read |\\n| One text file or independent reads together | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE [ABSOLUTE_FILE ...]`; up to eight selected inventoried inputs, the launcher-pinned task.md, or work files, at most 64 KiB output |\\n| Recover a truncated text read | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE --offset 0 --limit 4096`; one file, character offsets; continue from next_offset until complete is true |\\n\\nFor `instructions`, use canonical IDs such as `docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#read-this-when`. The earlier `released-resources/` inventory prefix also works. Request known sections together. The public reader includes the selected file's exact entry conditions when present; read their applicable references before acting. Inventory names are relative to the staged\\ninputs directory: `released-resources/docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`,\\n`source/src/greeting.py`, `client-help/create-artifact.txt`. **Do not add `inputs/`\\nto these names.** Native Read takes the absolute path, not an inventory name.\\nA digest or lookup is not a content read. Request known current\\nsections together and reuse unchanged content. Source inspection\\nis not test execution, and drafting a verification contract grants no execution\\nauthority.\\n\\n## Other operations\\n\\nRaw mode remains `remote OPERATION --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\nUse it for operations without typed input, or when explicitly checking a raw\\ncontract. Original schemas are under `reference/server/contracts/`. It takes no output flag. Copy those returned values\\nunchanged; do not compute or guess a replacement digest.\\n\\nUse `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` before the final report. Read its\\nselected fields as needed. `observed_content_reads` contains successful visible\\nread metadata; `file_reads` retains Claude Read attempts, including failures.\\nUse the observed trace instead of rebuilding it with inventory lookups.
